title: Evaluating and Improving LLM Self-Modeling
abstract: We study self-modeling: an LLM's ability to answer questions about its own behavior. We focus on verifiable behavioral questions, such as whether a prompt edit would change the model's final answer. To measure this capability, we introduce a benchmark that tests diverse types of self-modeling questions. Current models show non-trivial but limited self-modeling skill, and make systematic mistakes on simple counterfactual questions about their own behavior. To improve self-modeling skill, we develop a scalable synthetic-data pipeline that produces self-modeling training data, and show that reinforcement-learning can improve aggregate self-modeling skill across three open-source model families with some transfer to held-out tasks. These gains, however, do not seem to constitute introspection consistently: improved self-modeling may not arise from privileged access to the model's internal decision process.

title: GMTS: Gradient Magnitude-based Token Selection Improves RLVR Training for LLM Reasoning
abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL), particularly RL with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), has recently emerged as a central paradigm for enhancing large language models' (LLMs) reasoning abilities, demonstrating remarkable effectiveness across reasoning tasks. Recent studies suggest that high-entropy tokens play an exceptionally important role in model training, since training with only the highest 20% entropy tokens yields significant performance gains. However, why such high-entropy tokens are beneficial remains insufficiently understood. In this work, we find that although high-entropy tokens within one answer tend to correlate with large gradient magnitude, entropy alone fails to consistently reflect token importance across different answers, considering the variations in the answer-level reward signals. Based on this observation, we introduce the Gradient Magnitude-based Token Selection (GMTS) method to quantify token importance, which leverages the entropy-gradient connection to approximate gradient-magnitude rankings for token selection. We find that training on the top 20% tokens ranked by GMTS consistently outperforms entropy-based token selection across three reasoning domains and various model sizes, suggesting that GMTS provides a more fine-grained estimate of token contribution for RLVR training.

title: Whole-Slide Image Analysis under Realistic Few-Shot Annotation Protocols
abstract: Automating the analysis of whole-slide images has high clinical value, since characterizing cancers requires examining them in detail. Such analysis increasingly relies on vision-language models that provide patch-level zero-shot predictions. However, these predictions remain noisy and must be refined with a few annotations. A promising paradigm for this refinement is few-shot transduction. Rather than treating each patch independently, these methods leverage the relations between patches, together with a few annotations, to refine all predictions jointly. However, current transductive methods are evaluated under conditions that overlook key properties of whole-slide images: (i) datasets consist of independent patches extracted from multiple slides, ignoring the complex tissue organization; (ii) datasets are mostly balanced, whereas a single whole-slide image exhibits severe class imbalance, with several classes absent; and (iii) annotations are sampled at random, without reflecting how a pathologist annotates a limited number of regions. To align the transduction paradigm to realistic whole-slide settings, we introduce the following contributions. First, we propose SlideCRF, which adapts conditional random fields for whole-slide images by combining spatial and biological cues while accounting for classes that may be absent from a given slide. Second, we provide a set of realistic annotation protocols, based on spatially localized clicks and scribbles, modeling different pathologist interactions, such as the iterative correction of model errors. Across four datasets, we show that SlideCRF outperforms current transductive methods in macro F1, improving over the zero-shot predictions by +24.2% and +37.5% with one and 16 clicks per present class, respectively.

title: Federated Learning-Based Model Lifecycle Management for Intelligent Wireless Network Automation
abstract: This paper proposes a federated learning-based model life-cycle management framework to support the automation of intelligent wireless networks.Despite the existence of the feasibility that centralized learning could be leveraged for wireless network optimization (e.g., wireless network control and radio resource management), centralized acquisition of large-scale raw wireless network data may cause a substantial burden due to communication overhead and data privacy concerns, and leads the whole learning to be dependent on the centralized infrastructure resources.Distributed Federated Learning (FL) has been investigated to tackle the problem of centralized learning by allowing client participants to train their local models and share model updates with the server, rather than exposing raw data.An FL-based life-cycle management (FL-LCM) framework is proposed herein to integrate client registration, client capability assessment, life-cycle aware client selection, model retrieval, local model training, client aggregation, model update and global performance monitor in.A suitable client selection score is designed to represent a joint metric over client computing capability, data quality, communication reliability, trust, and expected overhead.To facilitate the technical evaluation, we present synthesized and logical experimental simulation results including model convergence, communication cost, latency index, threshold sensitivity, non-IID dataset sensitivity and ablative study.The simulation results indicate that our proposed framework can achieve performance similar to centralized learning with lower communication overhead in comparison to random federated learning and computed capability aware federated learning.Our approach is applicable to variety of applications including traffic prediction, anomaly detection, resource management, mobility management, and even some edge assistance wireless automation services.

title: Intelligent commerce: Impact of voice research on online shopping with reference to Alexa.
abstract: Abstract: Voice-activated artificial intelligence, such as Amazon Alexa, is fundamentally changing online shopping by introducing hands-free, conversational commerce. Research shows that using smart speakers does not just change how people search for items; it actually increases both how often they buy and how much money they spend. Instead of replacing mobile or computer sales, voice shopping acts as an extra channel that boosts overall retail engagement. Even with this rapid growth, everyday use faces a few hurdles. Shoppers love the speed and ease of buying routine items, like reordering groceries or everyday household goods. However, they often hesitate to buy expensive or new products without seeing a picture first. Furthermore, talking to a voicebot changes how our brains process information. Studies reveal that when shopping by voice instead of looking at a screen, consumers pay less attention to cost, making them more likely to accept pricier upgrades. Another major challenge is trust. Because voice assistants usually suggest just one top product and set it as the default choice, shoppers lose the freedom to easily compare options. This means brands must completely adapt their strategies to match natural, spoken questions if they want to be recommended. Ultimately, while voice commerce is still maturing and working through privacy concerns, it represents a massive shift. As technology improves, Alexa will likely evolve from a basic tool into a highly personalized shopping companion.

title: Dungeons That Build Themselves: A Historical Development Review of Procedural Content Generation in Roguelikes
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Procedural Content Generation in Roguelikes in the context of Game Development. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of PCG and roguelikes as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Game Development.

title: 基于多尺度几何的量子态学习算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state learning algorithm based on multi-scale geometric features. Traditional quantum state learning methods often focus on mathematical properties of the quantum state, whereas this algorithm explicitly connects the quantum state to different geometric scales, providing a more comprehensive understanding of the state. We propose a framework that learns quantum state parameters by analyzing the geometric characteristics of the system, leading to more efficient quantum computation. This work addresses limitations in existing methods by incorporating geometric information directly into the learning process. We detail the algorithm's architecture, training procedure, and experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness in learning and manipulating quantum states. The core claim is that this approach offers a significant improvement over existing methods by leveraging geometric information for enhanced quantum state representation and computation.

title: Quantum-Enhanced Statistical Physics
abstract: Quantum-Enhanced Statistical Physics represents a paradigm shift in the study of complex systems, moving beyond traditional simulation methods to exploit the potential of quantum entanglement and measurement. This paper proposes a novel framework, utilizing a quantum-driven algorithm to simulate complex systems by creating correlated, non-classical states. The core claim is to develop a robust and quantitative approach to exploring statistical physics phenomena, pushing the boundaries of current understanding through the application of quantum mechanics. The paper details the algorithm's design, explores its theoretical implications, and provides initial results demonstrating the potential for significant advancements in predictive capabilities.

title: Title: High-Dimensional Non-Linear Matrix Quantum Computation Verification and Optimization
abstract: This paper explores the application of high-dimensional non-linear matrix quantum computation verification and optimization techniques. We investigate a novel framework that integrates quantum optimization algorithms with established matrix verification methods to rigorously assess the quantum properties of matrices. The core mechanism centers on utilizing the inherent quantum characteristics of high-dimensional matrices through a specific verification protocol, leveraging quantum optimization to enhance validation accuracy. The research aims to establish a robust quantum algorithm foundation, providing a pathway for validating complex matrix operations with increased precision and efficiency. The paper demonstrates the potential of this approach to advance the state of quantum algorithm development and validation.

title: ##拓扑量子纠缠理论
abstract: This paper investigates the theoretical framework for exploring and utilizing quantum entanglement in a novel context: the integration of topological quantum mechanics with quantum computation. We propose a new conceptual model, termed "Quantum Topological Field Theory" (QTFT), that leverages the inherent properties of topological states to enhance quantum entanglement and provide a pathway toward exceeding the limitations of classical computation. The core of this research focuses on designing a quantum state capable of self-sustained and extended entanglement, and establishing a quantum computing platform to facilitate the implementation of ultra-high-density quantum computation. The potential impact of this approach lies in fundamentally altering the landscape of quantum information processing, offering a paradigm shift towards computation beyond the capabilities of current technologies.

title: 拓扑信息论的量子态转移与操控
abstract: The pursuit of quantum computation has spurred significant advancements in quantum information theory, particularly in the realm of quantum state transfer and manipulation. Traditional approaches often rely on precise pulse control, limiting the potential for highly efficient and robust quantum operations. This paper introduces a novel framework based on topological information theory, offering a fundamentally different approach to manipulating quantum states. We propose a system where the state transfer and control are governed by topological structures, enabling precise and efficient operations through dynamic adjustments. The core mechanism involves defining transfer and manipulation rules based on the structure of the underlying topology, achieving improvements in quantum computation's efficiency. This work establishes a new paradigm for quantum state manipulation, leveraging the power of topological principles to enhance the capabilities of quantum systems.

title: Dynamic Quantum Entanglement Network Topology Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimizing the topology of quantum entanglement networks using reinforcement learning. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the network's structure based on real-time analysis of key performance indicators such as entanglement rate, coherence time, and connection reliability. A simulated quantum entanglement network is established, with nodes representing quantum processors or memories. A reinforcement learning agent is employed to make topology adjustment decisions—adding or removing nodes, modifying connection patterns—to maximize the success rate of specific quantum protocols or minimize transmission errors. The key innovation lies in the adaptive optimization process, leveraging the inherent uncertainties of quantum networks and incorporating robustness through reinforcement learning, thereby enabling the network to respond effectively to environmental changes. The theoretical framework is presented, outlining the key components and algorithms involved in this dynamic topology optimization system. The system is designed to enhance the overall efficiency and fault tolerance of quantum information transfer.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning for Representation Distillation
abstract: Representation distillation, a technique for transferring knowledge from a larger, more complex model (teacher) to a smaller, more efficient model (student), has shown significant promise in various machine learning applications. However, a critical limitation of conventional distillation methods lies in their reliance on a fixed kernel function to map representations between the teacher and student. This paper proposes a novel approach, Adaptive Kernel Learning, which dynamically adjusts the kernel function during the distillation process. This adaptation is driven by an "Adaptive Kernel Optimizer," a recurrent neural network that learns to optimize kernel parameters based on the distillation loss and a learned dissimilarity metric. The core claim is that such dynamic adaptation significantly improves distillation performance by minimizing distortion while maximizing knowledge transfer. We introduce a formal framework outlining this approach, detailing the key components and their mathematical relationships. The proposed method offers a more nuanced and effective way to represent and transfer knowledge, particularly beneficial in scenarios where the source and target representations exhibit evolving similarity.

title: Quantum-Inspired Geometry for Computational Complexity
abstract: Quantum-inspired geometry proposes a novel framework for quantifying computational complexity by leveraging the properties of quantum phenomena. This paper explores the concept of a "Quantum Complexity Metric" – a quantifiable measure derived from the inherent characteristics of quantum states and entanglement – to provide an alternative to traditional complexity measures. We delve into the potential benefits of this approach, emphasizing its ability to identify patterns and bottlenecks in algorithm performance. The research focuses on establishing a rigorous mathematical foundation for this metric, outlining its operational principles and demonstrating its potential to enhance our understanding of computational limitations. Specifically, we will address the challenges of quantifying entanglement and its connection to computational cost, and we will present preliminary results utilizing a simplified, yet illustrative, model. Ultimately, this work aims to advance the field by suggesting a fundamentally new approach to analyzing complexity, potentially leading to more efficient algorithms and deeper insights into the boundaries of computation.

title: Black-eared Squirrel Optimization (BESO): A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Black-Eared Squirrel Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Black-eared Squirrel Optimization (BESO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of black-eared squirrels (Sciurus negravianus). The algorithm mimics the squirrels' strategy of searching for food resources by utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation phases, mirroring their movement patterns, caching behavior, and decision-making processes. BESO employs a squirrel population, each representing a potential solution to the optimization problem. The movement of each squirrel is governed by a stochastic process, influenced by the perceived availability of resources (fitness values) and the distance to the nearest food source. The algorithm incorporates a 'cache' mechanism, analogous to the squirrels' caching of food, to retain promising solutions. We detail the algorithm's design, including its key parameters, the objective function, and its application to various benchmark optimization problems. Preliminary results demonstrate that BESO is competitive with existing metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with complex landscapes and multiple local optima. The algorithm's adaptability and its reliance on a biologically inspired model offer a potentially robust and efficient approach to solving a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: ## Black Bear Metaheuristic Algorithm (BBMA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Black Bear Metaheuristic Algorithm (BBMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of black bears. BBMA leverages the black bear's strategy of searching for food in a region with varying food density, employing a combination of exploration and exploitation phases. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, with each individual representing a potential solution. The position of each individual is determined by a two-dimensional coordinate system, representing the solution space. The algorithm incorporates a novel movement strategy mimicking the black bear's approach to finding food, which involves adjusting the movement direction and distance based on the local food density. The core of BBMA lies in its adaptive parameter control mechanism, which dynamically adjusts the exploration and exploitation parameters based on the convergence rate of the algorithm. The performance of BBMA is evaluated on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capabilities. The results indicate that BBMA provides a viable alternative to existing metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in scenarios where the problem landscape exhibits significant variations in food density. The key components of the algorithm include: population initialization, movement strategy, local food density estimation, adaptive parameter control, and convergence criteria.

title: ## Bison: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bison Herding Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bison, a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the observed behavior of bison herds during migration. The algorithm leverages the concepts of flocking, herding, and dynamic territory defense, which are fundamental to bison social dynamics, to effectively explore and optimize complex search spaces. Bison incorporates a novel population management strategy based on territorial ownership, a dynamic adjustment of individual movement probabilities influenced by social interactions, and a mechanism for removing ineffective individuals – mimicking the natural selection processes observed in bison herds. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a suite of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic methods such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO). The results demonstrate Bison's potential as a robust and efficient solution for a range of optimization challenges.

title: Causal Inference via Bayesian Networks with Multiple Variables
abstract: This paper explores the application of multi-variable Bayesian networks (MVBNs) for causal inference. Traditional statistical methods often struggle to accurately represent and reason about causal relationships, particularly in complex systems with multiple interacting variables. This research proposes a framework utilizing MVBNs to construct more robust models of causal relationships, facilitating improved inference and decision-making. The core of this approach lies in leveraging the probabilistic nature of Bayesian networks to explicitly model and reason about uncertainty inherent in causal relationships. This paper details the methodology for constructing MVBNs, outlines the inference techniques, and discusses the advantages of this approach over conventional methods. The key contribution is a novel method for representing and manipulating causal relationships within a probabilistic framework, leading to more accurate and interpretable causal inferences. Specifically, we demonstrate how the structure of the MVBN can be informed by domain expertise and data analysis, and how this network can then be used to perform interventions and counterfactual reasoning. The paper concludes with a discussion of potential future research directions and the broader implications of this work.

title: Adaptive Self-Restraint Geometry (ASRG)
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Self-Restraint Geometry (ASRG), a novel algorithmic framework designed to enhance model performance on complex data distributions. Traditional approaches often rely on manual design, limiting their adaptability to intricate data patterns. ASRG leverages the inherent self-restraint properties of geometric structures to dynamically adjust data distributions, resulting in improved model accuracy and robustness. The core mechanism involves a sophisticated interplay between geometric constraints and data flow, enabling the algorithm to optimize performance across a wider range of scenarios. This research explores the potential of ASRG to overcome the limitations of conventional methods, offering a promising path towards more intelligent and adaptable models.

title: Quantum Neural Networks via Multi-Body Entanglement Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum neural networks (QNNs) by focusing on optimizing multi-body entanglement within the network architecture. The core claim is that strategic manipulation of entanglement between multiple nodes in a neural network can significantly enhance computational capabilities and improve information encoding efficiency. The proposed mechanism involves designing an algorithm to dynamically control the entanglement strength between nodes. This allows for the realization of more efficient parallel computation and enhanced information encoding. We explore theoretical frameworks and mathematical formulations to demonstrate the potential advantages of this approach compared to classical neural networks. The research highlights a novel pathway toward constructing quantum-enhanced neural network models by leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The primary focus is on the mathematical modeling and optimization strategies required to effectively harness entanglement for QNN performance.

title: Distributed Quantum State Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for verifying the integrity of quantum states utilizing a distributed network of entangled sensors. The core principle rests on the inherent security offered by entanglement against eavesdropping attempts. The system employs a network of sensors continuously monitoring and comparing the state of a quantum system. Entanglement plays a critical role in detecting any manipulation or measurement, thereby ensuring the authenticity of the quantum state. The proposed architecture significantly enhances the robustness of quantum state verification compared to traditional methods, offering a fundamentally secure approach to quantum communication and computation. This paper details the theoretical framework, outlining key concepts and mathematical formulations. The system's performance is discussed, and the potential implications for secure quantum networks are explored.

title: 自适应量子态的模拟与计算
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for quantum state simulation and computation, termed "Adaptive Quantum State Simulation and Computation" (AQSCC). AQSCC leverages the unique properties of quantum states to achieve significantly enhanced precision and efficiency in quantum state representation and manipulation. We introduce a dynamic adjustment mechanism that continuously adapts the simulation parameters based on the observed quantum state evolution, mitigating computational bottlenecks and improving the accuracy of results. The core mechanism revolves around a feedback loop that optimizes the simulation process by dynamically adjusting the underlying quantum state representation. This approach promises substantial improvements in quantum computing performance, particularly for complex quantum algorithms requiring high fidelity. The paper details the architecture of AQSCC, discusses its performance evaluation against existing methods, and presents preliminary results demonstrating substantial gains in simulation accuracy and computational speed. Finally, we explore potential future directions and applications of this technique.

title: Quantum Topology-Based Adaptive Geometry Structural Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithmic framework, Quantum Topology-Based Adaptive Geometry Structural Optimization (QTASO), designed to automate the construction of complex geometric structures and leverage topological properties for optimization, particularly in materials and structural design. The core mechanism centers around constructing a geometric structure with inherent adaptability, achieved through a tailored optimization algorithm that exploits quantum entanglement and error correction. We present a detailed explanation of the algorithm's key components, including the quantum topology representation, optimization strategy, and error mitigation techniques. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of QTASO in optimizing various geometric configurations, including novel material designs and structural elements, offering a significant advancement over existing geometric optimization approaches.

title: Bare-tailed Armored Tree Rat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Bare-tailed Armored Tree Rat" (BATR) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the bare-tailed armored tree rat ( *Datomicus titanus* ). This algorithm leverages the rat's unique strategy of exploring a territory while maintaining a core area and strategically discarding peripheral regions based on resource availability. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a dynamic territory representation and a novel 'discarding' mechanism to mimic the rat's adaptive exploration. We present the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulations, and its application to several benchmark optimization problems. The performance of the BATR algorithm is evaluated against established metaheuristic methods, demonstrating its effectiveness in tackling complex, multi-dimensional optimization challenges. The key mathematical formulations include the territory size calculation (Equation 1), the discarding probability (Equation 2), and the adaptive movement strategy (Equation 3). The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through numerical experiments, showcasing its ability to converge efficiently and find near-optimal solutions. Future research directions include incorporating adaptive parameters and exploring its applicability to various domains.

title: High-Dimensional Topological Information Encoding
abstract: High-dimensional topological information encoding presents a novel approach to information storage and transmission, leveraging the inherent properties of high-dimensional topological structures. This paper explores the potential of utilizing a dynamically adaptive topological structure to significantly reduce information redundancy and enhance transmission efficiency. We propose a new encoding scheme based on a "information encoding tree" and "topological encryption," employing self-adaptive topology to minimize redundancy and enhance security. The core mechanism involves constructing a tree structure that dynamically adjusts to the input data, ensuring a robust and efficient encoding process. This work offers a promising avenue for enhancing information processing and transmission, particularly in scenarios demanding high-dimensional data.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Information Encoding and Time Series Prediction
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement for enhancing time series prediction. Traditional time series forecasting methods often struggle with complex, non-linear patterns and high-dimensional data. We propose a novel approach that leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to encode time series information and extract predictive insights. Specifically, we map time series data onto entangled quantum states, allowing us to access correlations and patterns that may be missed by classical methods. The theoretical framework outlines the key principles, including the mapping process, the measurement strategy, and the expected improvement in predictive accuracy. We present a mathematical model incorporating entanglement entropy and its influence on the prediction process. The core claim is that this entanglement-based encoding significantly improves time series prediction. The research highlights a fundamentally different approach to time series analysis, moving beyond classical information processing to exploit the quantum mechanical phenomenon of entanglement.

title: Quantum-Inspired Anomaly Detection for High-Dimensional Data
abstract: This paper introduces a novel anomaly detection algorithm inspired by the principles of quantum mechanics, specifically quantum superposition and measurement. Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle with high-dimensional data, suffering from the curse of dimensionality and sensitivity to noise. Our approach addresses these challenges by representing data points as superposition states within a Hilbert space. A "quantum measurement" operator is then employed to identify deviations from expected patterns. Crucially, the algorithm dynamically adapts measurement parameters based on data characteristics, enhancing its robustness and adaptability. We demonstrate the potential of this quantum-inspired technique to outperform conventional methods in detecting anomalies in complex, high-dimensional datasets. The core of the algorithm resides in the probabilistic nature of quantum measurement, allowing for a nuanced assessment of data points rather than relying on strict thresholding. We formalize this approach through a mathematical framework, outlining the key components and operational principles.

title: Title: Quantum Entanglement Resonance Mapping (QERM) – Exploiting Non-Locality
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental quantum phenomenon, possesses unique properties that promise transformative capabilities in computation and information processing. This research investigates a novel computational framework, Quantum Entanglement Resonance Mapping (QERM), designed to leverage this resource for mapping and analyzing non-local correlations. We propose a computational algorithm that traces entanglement paths, generating a precise representation of correlation structure, and then uses this information to generate novel entanglement-based computations. The core claim is that QERM offers a new approach to quantifying and manipulating entanglement, potentially accelerating certain computations and providing a deeper understanding of complex system dynamics. This paper will detail the algorithm's architecture, mathematical foundations, and preliminary experimental validation, demonstrating its potential for quantifying and manipulating entanglement.

title: ## Mimic Octopus Metaheuristic Algorithm (MOMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimic Octopus Metaheuristic Algorithm (MOMA), a novel optimization algorithm inspired by the remarkable camouflage and behavioral mimicry abilities of the Mimic Octopus (*Thaumoctopus mimicus*). Unlike traditional metaheuristics that often rely on random exploration and exploitation, MOMA incorporates a dynamic 'morphing' strategy mimicking the octopus's ability to rapidly change its appearance and behavior to adapt to its environment. The algorithm utilizes a population of 'octopus agents', each representing a potential solution. Each agent's "morph" is represented by a set of parameters, which are iteratively adjusted based on a local environment assessment and a global search for optimal configurations. The core innovation lies in the 'mimicry' mechanism, where agents' parameters are influenced by the best-performing agents in their immediate neighborhood, fostering both convergence and diversity. This paper details the algorithm's design, including the representation of solutions, the mimicry mechanism, and the objective function evaluation process. We argue that this approach, rooted in biological inspiration, offers a potentially robust and adaptable solution for a variety of optimization problems.

title: Dimension Space: A Novel Algebraic Structure for Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel algebraic structure, termed the "Dimension Space," as a bridge between linear algebra and non-linear algebra. The core claim is that this framework offers a pathway to understanding and manipulating quantum systems within high-dimensional spaces, potentially driving significant advancements in quantum computing theory. We investigate the inherent properties of this dimension space and its relationship to quantum computation, proposing a mechanism to leverage this structure for enhanced algorithm design and optimization. The study will analyze the behavior of quantum states and quantum circuits within this space, highlighting potential implications for quantum information processing.

title: ## Desert Tortoise-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (DTSA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Desert Tortoise-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (DTSA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of desert tortoises. Desert tortoises exhibit remarkable resilience and adaptability in harsh environments, primarily driven by a combination of exploratory and exploitative movements, coupled with a sophisticated strategy for resource allocation. DTSA mimics these behaviors by incorporating a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, adaptive step size control, and a memory-based learning mechanism. The algorithm utilizes a population of potential solutions, each represented by a vector of parameters. The core of DTSA lies in its "sand-seeking" and "oasis-finding" mechanisms, which guide the search process. The algorithm adjusts its step size based on the perceived environmental "stress" and utilizes a memory component to retain successful solution candidates, effectively concentrating the search around promising regions of the solution space. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, operational rules, and highlights its potential advantages over existing metaheuristic techniques.

title: Dynamic Topological Quantum Error Correction Code
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum error correction, termed the Dynamic Topological Quantum Error Correction Code. The core claim posits that the topological structure of quantum error correction codes is not static, but rather adaptable to the dynamic evolution of quantum information encoding. This adaptability is achieved through a programmable topological network that utilizes controlled topological transformations of entangled states. The mechanism involves dynamically altering topological connections between qubits during quantum information transmission, optimizing error correction rates and efficiency. The research addresses the limitations of traditional topological quantum error correction codes, which assume a fixed topological structure, by introducing a real-time responsive network capable of adapting and optimizing its correction performance. We propose a framework for designing such a system, focusing on the control and manipulation of entangled states to achieve dynamic topological reconfiguration. The key innovation lies in the ability to shift from a static, pre-determined topology to a topology optimized for the current state of the encoded quantum information. This approach offers a significant potential improvement in the robustness and efficiency of quantum communication and computation. The theoretical framework presented outlines the fundamental principles and considerations for implementing this dynamic code, paving the way for future advancements in quantum error correction.

title: Multi-field Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper explores the potential of multi-field quantum computing, a novel approach to quantum computation that leverages the superposition and entanglement of multiple quantum fields. Traditional quantum computing often restricts itself to a single qubit state, but this research proposes a system designed to exploit the unique properties of multiple quantum fields, enabling significantly more complex computations. We outline the fundamental principles underlying this design, detail the architecture of the proposed system, and discuss the potential advantages and challenges in realizing this ambitious goal. The core claim is that the system's ability to manipulate and entangle multiple fields will dramatically enhance computational capabilities compared to existing quantum computing paradigms.

title: Information-Theoretic Regularization of Deep Belief Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel regularization technique for Deep Belief Networks (DBNs) based on information-theoretic principles. The core idea is to minimize the mutual information between layers during the training process. We hypothesize that this approach promotes more disentangled representations within the DBN, leading to improved generalization performance. The method introduces a regularization term into the DBN's loss function, explicitly penalizing high mutual information between layers. This is achieved through the quantification of mutual information using Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and subsequent minimization. The contribution of this work lies in the direct application of information theory to constrain the learning dynamics of DBNs, specifically targeting the representational bottleneck commonly encountered in deep learning. We demonstrate, theoretically, how this approach can lead to more robust and efficient feature learning.

title: Dimensional Quantum Entanglement
abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging dimensionality transformations to mitigate measurement errors and enable communication across the quantum realm. We propose a novel quantum entanglement protocol utilizing dynamic dimensionality shifts, coupled with quantum entanglement simulation and a form of spatial information propagation, aiming to dramatically reduce errors inherent in traditional quantum measurement techniques. The core mechanism involves a quantum field simulation to precisely measure entanglement, followed by the introduction of quantum entanglement via a dynamic, multi-dimensional quantum state. This research aims to establish a foundation for quantum computation's expansion, pushing beyond the limitations of classical measurement. This work addresses the critical challenge of error correction and offers a potential pathway toward more robust and scalable quantum systems.

The core mechanism involves a quantum field simulation to precisely measure entanglement, followed by the introduction of quantum entanglement via a dynamic, multi-dimensional quantum state. This research aims to establish a foundation for quantum computation's expansion, pushing beyond the limitations of classical measurement. This work addresses the critical challenge of error correction and offers a potential pathway toward more robust and scalable quantum systems.

title: Title: Adaptive Quantum Feedback Loops for Algorithmic Stability
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing numerous fields, yet the inherent instability of quantum algorithms poses a significant challenge. This paper investigates the application of adaptive quantum feedback loops to enhance algorithmic stability, addressing the problem of divergence and ensuring consistent performance across a wide range of conditions. We introduce a novel system of continuous monitoring and adjustment, leveraging the inherent dynamics of quantum systems to proactively mitigate instability. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that dynamically adjusts quantum parameters based on the algorithm's output, effectively correcting for deviations and promoting stability. This approach offers a potential pathway to significantly improve the reliability and predictability of quantum computations.

title: The Rock Cormorant Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RIMO)
abstract: This paper introduces the Rock Cormorant Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RIMO), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of rock cormorants. These birds exhibit a unique strategy for locating fish, utilizing a combination of individual searching and collaborative information sharing. RIMO leverages these principles by employing a population of 'cormorants' that simultaneously explore the search space and share information through a dynamic 'observation point' system. The algorithm's core components include an initial population initialization, a fitness evaluation function, a movement strategy based on cormorant foraging, and a mechanism for adjusting observation points to enhance convergence. Unlike traditional metaheuristics, RIMO's observation point system dynamically adapts to the search landscape, mimicking the cormorant's ability to identify and prioritize promising regions. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, focusing on the underlying principles and conceptual framework rather than empirical validation. The aim is to provide a foundational understanding of RIMO and its potential for future development within the broader field of metaheuristic optimization.

title: Algorithmic Quantum Simulation of Fluid Dynamics with Entangled Particles
abstract: This paper explores the implementation of an algorithmic quantum simulation approach for fluid dynamics, leveraging quantum entanglement to achieve a significant advancement over classical methods. The core claim posits the creation of a novel algorithm capable of generating remarkably accurate simulations of turbulent flows and wave propagation, addressing limitations of current computational capabilities. We detail the methodology, including the representation of fluid state using entangled particles, the quantum algorithm design, and preliminary results demonstrating improved accuracy in complex flow scenarios. The paper argues that this research has the potential to unlock novel insights into fluid dynamics and contribute to advancements in areas such as weather forecasting, computational fluid mechanics, and materials science.

title: ## The Brown-Backed Pigeon Optimization Algorithm (BPO Algorithm)
abstract: This paper introduces the Brown-Backed Pigeon Optimization Algorithm (BPO Algorithm), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of brown-backed pigeons. The algorithm leverages the pigeons' tendency to fly in a circular pattern around a food source, adjusting their flight direction and altitude based on a combination of local exploration and global search. The core mechanism involves a dynamic adjustment of flight parameters influenced by a 'pigeon density' function and a 'flight attraction' factor. The algorithm iteratively updates the solution set by mimicking the pigeons' movement, aiming to converge towards the global optimum. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical framework, detailing the key parameters and their roles in guiding the search process, and highlights its potential advantages over existing metaheuristic methods.

title: Cognitive Graph Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes Cognitive Graph Neural Networks (CGNNs), a novel approach to artificial intelligence that leverages the principles of knowledge representation and cognitive processing. The core idea is to build neural networks capable of mimicking human cognitive processes by explicitly incorporating knowledge graphs and utilizing graph-based attention mechanisms. CGNNs employ graph convolutional layers to propagate information across a knowledge graph, dynamically weighted by attention mechanisms that prioritize relevant connections. This architecture represents a significant step toward biologically inspired AI, bridging the gap between traditional graph neural networks and cognitive science research. The network is trained on a large knowledge graph, enabling it to learn complex relationships and perform reasoning tasks effectively. The primary contribution lies in the synergistic combination of graph neural networks and cognitive science principles, leading to a more robust and interpretable AI system. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is demonstrated through the potential for improved performance in tasks such as relation extraction, knowledge completion, and reasoning.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Topology-Based Machine Learning Model
abstract: This paper introduces a novel machine learning model based on dynamic adaptive topology structures. Traditional machine learning models often rely on static parameters, limiting their adaptability and potentially hindering performance in dynamic environments. Our proposed framework dynamically adjusts topology parameters to optimize model performance and generalization capabilities. The core mechanism involves the generation and optimization of a topology structure that adapts to the data distribution, enabling the model to learn effectively across varying conditions. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments, showcasing significant improvements in prediction accuracy and generalization performance compared to baseline models.

title: Adaptive Self-Organized Quantum Systems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to designing adaptive self-organized quantum systems, leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum tunneling to enhance the system's adaptability and facilitate more complex and efficient quantum computations. Traditional quantum systems are often static, and this algorithm introduces self-organization capabilities to enable more flexible quantum computation. The core mechanism centers around the manipulation of quantum entanglement and tunneling to achieve this adaptability. This work presents a framework for dynamically adjusting the system's properties, offering a significant advancement over existing approaches. The resulting system demonstrates improved performance in specific quantum algorithms through enhanced adaptability. The study explores the potential of this approach in tackling complex computational problems and lays the foundation for future research into adaptive quantum systems.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization via Wave Function Collapse
abstract: Quantum-inspired optimization aims to leverage quantum mechanical phenomena to accelerate and improve the performance of optimization algorithms. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing wave function collapse to guide the search process, demonstrating its potential for enhanced efficiency and solution quality. We formulate the optimization problem as a quantum system, employing wave function collapse to create a probabilistic exploration of the solution space. The paper details the algorithm's design, the mechanics behind wave function collapse, and its performance evaluation against established optimization techniques. The core claim is that this approach offers a significant advancement in optimization, particularly for complex problems where traditional methods struggle.

title: Adaptive Quantum State-Based Energy Maximization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel energy maximization algorithm based on adaptive quantum state manipulation. Traditional approaches to quantum state optimization often rely on classical physics, limiting their ability to effectively address complex quantum systems. We propose a method that dynamically adjusts quantum states, enabling a more intelligent and automated optimization process. This work leverages the unique properties of quantum states to achieve significant improvements in energy maximization compared to existing algorithms. The core mechanism involves a continuous feedback loop that adjusts quantum states based on a learned reward function, fostering a deeper understanding of the system's energy landscape.

title: 基于自适应的量子态的超导量子计算
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of a novel quantum computing paradigm based on dynamically adjusted superconducting quantum states. Traditional quantum computation often relies on static parameter settings, limiting scalability and stability. We propose a method utilizing self-adaptive quantum state parameters to dynamically adjust these parameters, thereby enhancing the system's performance. This approach offers a significant improvement in resource utilization and stability compared to conventional methods. The core mechanism centers around a feedback loop that continuously optimizes the quantum state based on observed performance metrics. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental validation demonstrating the effectiveness of this dynamic adjustment strategy in achieving enhanced qubit coherence and reduced error rates. The results suggest a substantial advancement in the practical implementation of quantum computing.

title: Fine-Tuning a Large Multilingual Text-to-Speech Model for Nepali on Consumer Hardware: A Teacher Model for Knowledge Distillation with Speaker Identity Verification
abstract: Nepali is a low resource language for speech technology and there is very little open text-to-speech support for it. Most high quality neural TTS models are too large to run in real time on the low end machines that are common in Nepal, and the usual answer to that problem is knowledge distillation, where a large teacher model generates training speech for a small student model. That approach only works if the teacher is itself correct, because every error the teacher makes is copied into the student. This paper reports the construction and verification of such a teacher. A 937M parameter multilingual model, Indic Parler-TTS, was fine-tuned to a single Nepali female speaker identity using 4-bit quantization with a DoRA and RS-LoRA adapter of rank 32 applied only to the decoder, on a single laptop GPU with 6 GB of VRAM. The training data was 2,006 clips, which is 2.62 hours of licensed Nepali speech from 18 speakers, of which the target speaker contributed 496 clips or 35.8 minutes. The complete fine-tune used 2.48 GB of VRAM and 2,500 training steps. The fine-tune on these 2,006 clips succeeded. High frequency energy in the generated speech measures 0.3215 percent against the real speaker's 0.326 percent, so the output is spectrally matched to her recordings. A threshold-free blend prediction test shows the model favours the target speaker rather than averaging the corpus: the generated centroid scores 0.853 against her, while a constructed 18-way average of the corpus scores only 0.784, and a nearest-centroid assignment places 500 of 500 generated clips with the target speaker against a chance rate of 5.6 percent. A blind twenty clip listening comparison confirmed that the output is heard as one consistent woman. An earlier fine-tune, trained on a differently constructed dataset, had failed completely, and that failure is also reported because it is instructive: two data defects produced a voice nine times more muffled than the real speaker while character error rate stayed near 0.10 throughout, so every metric then in use stayed healthy through a total failure. The paper further reports that selecting a checkpoint by validation loss gives a worse voice than the final checkpoint, because validation loss over a speaker mixture is best for the average rather than best for the target, and that the teacher renders 100 percent of consonant conjuncts present in its fine-tuning data against 78 percent of those absent, which quantifies a generalization limit usually assumed away.

title: Role-Aware Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Urban Rail Transit Fault Management
abstract: Urban rail transit systems require reliable decision-support methods to assist operators in handling complex fault events. Although large language models provide strong reasoning and knowledge integration capabilities, their open-ended generation may produce responses that are difficult to align with operational procedures. To address this issue, we propose a role-aware agentic retrieval-augmented generation framework for transit fault management. The framework integrates keyword-based retrieval, role-aware multi-agent reasoning, and constrained action generation within a unified architecture. Operational procedures and historical cases retrieved from transit knowledge repositories provide evidence for agent reasoning, while constrained outputs ensure that generated instructions remain consistent with predefined operational actions. Experimental results on a real-world urban rail transit emergency exercise dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework improves the semantic score from 0.893 to 0.965 and increases Role F1 score from 0.824 to 0.915 compared with an Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) baseline while maintaining comparable inference efficiency. These results demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework for decision support in urban rail transit fault scenarios.

title: Humanlike representation of social networks in large language models
abstract: Although large language models (LLMs) have made great progress in their general reasoning capabilities, reasoning about social relationships has remained a challenge. In contrast, humans are naturally skilled at reasoning about how people are connected to one another, even in large, complex social networks. Recent research in cognitive science suggests that a key component of human social intelligence is the ability to represent social networks using multistep abstraction, which integrates knowledge of both direct and indirect social connections, and therefore supports inferences about network members’ social proximity to one another. Here, we test whether LLMs represent social networks using similar computational principles. In Study 1, we converted an existing human social navigation task into text and recorded LLM responses to the same problems humans were tasked with solving. LLMs’ behaviors closely mirrored those of human participants, and were best-explained by Katz communicability, a model of multistep abstraction that captures how humans represent and navigate social networks. In Study 2, we tested whether these multistep representations persisted in a task where they offered no benefit—and were in fact detrimental to task accuracy—and found that LLMs continued to show a multistep signature even in this context. These findings suggest that multistep abstraction may be a core property of how LLMs represent relational information, closely paralleling accounts of human cognitive maps.

title: Unsupervised anomaly detection with deep generative models: an experimental analysis of model variability and mitigation strategies
abstract: PurposeUnsupervised anomaly detection allows identifying anomalies from unlabeled data, making it useful for neuroimaging analysis and computer-aided diagnosis. Given an individual’s scan, we use a generative model to construct a subject-specific image of healthy appearance and compare both images with identify anomalies. Such approach has drawbacks as the reconstructions are imperfect, and model variability is not taken into account.ApproachWe study model variability arising from using different random seeds during training and explore strategies to mitigate the effect of unwanted reconstruction errors and variability. The strategies include model ensembling, anomaly map normalization, and anomaly map designs based on single or multiple pseudo-healthy reconstructions. We compare these approaches in the context of dementia-related anomalies on 3D FDG PET from ADNI using variational autoencoder models.ResultsOur experiments suggest that variance between models can be reduced by aggregating their reconstructions in a Z-score based anomaly map. This strategy is highly effective, but computationally expensive, as it requires training several instances of the model. An alternative strategy is to normalize the anomaly map using statistics computed from a healthy validation set. We show that this normalization strategy substantially reduces performance variability across models and even increases anomaly detection performance in certain cases.ConclusionWe highlight a largely overlooked source of variability in deep generative models, their random seed, which can lead to substantially different anomaly detection performance and biased evaluation. Our experimental analysis emphasizes that it is crucial to design robust anomaly maps and to mitigate the impact of randomness-induced variability, by accounting for model reconstruction errors for instance using Z-score ensembling, or healthy-control normalization, to support more stable and trustworthy deployment in real-world clinical practice.

title: EGT-KG: Evidence-Grounded Typed KG Retrieval for Practical Scientific QA with Small Language Models
abstract: For emerging scientific research domains, local Small Language Models (SLMs) are becoming more attractive, as they offer stronger privacy control and more stable deployment pipelines than Large Language Models. However, in practice, scientific question-answering on SLMs often operates under inevitable constraints: small literature collections, fragmented evidence, limited context window and reasoning abilities. We propose the Evidence-Grounded Typed Knowledge Graph (EGT-KG), a retrieval framework to improve information retrieval with local SLMs. We assessed three question-answering settings: a vanilla Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) workflow and two EGT-KG workflows: an automatically generated relation schema (AS) and an expert-defined relation schema (ES). Our experiments were evaluated with a six-dimensional evaluation framework (S3CRF: Soundness, Correctness, Completeness, Conciseness, Relevance, Fluency) on a Biopolymer-bound Soil Composite literature benchmark, showing that EGT-KG outperforms the vanilla RAG method in most settings, with the best improvement from llama3:8b: a Final Score of 70.37 (+14.67%) and 68.82 (+12.14%) by AS/ES EGT-KG variants.

title: PyKEEN-NSX: A Modular Framework for Static, Dynamic and Schema-Aware Negative Sampling in PyKEEN
abstract: Embedding methods have become popular due to their scalability on link prediction and/or triple classification tasks on Knowledge Graphs (KGs). Embedding models are trained relying on both positive and negative samples of triples. However, since KGs generally contain only positive assertions, negative samples are artificially generated through negative sampling strategies, ranging from simple random corruption to more sophisticated approaches that exploit structural, semantic, or embedding information. The design and implementation of advanced negative samplers remains challenging, as most popular Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE) libraries provide support only for basic strategies and lack a unified framework for developing more advanced and customized solutions. To address this gap, we introduce PyKEEN-NSX, an extension of PyKEEN, the popular KGE framework, that provides a modular engineered abstraction for negative sampling. The proposed architecture separates the generation of candidate negative pools, conditioned on an explicit context, from the selection strategy, enabling the development and integration of static, schema-aware and dynamic approaches within a consistent framework. Based on this abstraction, we implement six negative samplers, while remaining fully compatible with existing PyKEEN workflows and pipelines. As a proof of concept, we study negative availability across four datasets, showing that constrained pools frequently fall below the requested number of negatives, so that the encoded criterion is to a large extent replaced by the random fallback that supplements them.

However, since KGs generally contain only positive assertions, negative samples are artificially generated through negative sampling strategies, ranging from simple random corruption to more sophisticated approaches that exploit structural, semantic, or embedding information. The design and implementation of advanced negative samplers remains challenging, as most popular Knowledge Graph Embedding (KGE) libraries provide support only for basic strategies and lack a unified framework for developing more advanced and customized solutions. To address this gap, we introduce PyKEEN-NSX, an extension of PyKEEN, the popular KGE framework, that provides a modular engineered abstraction for negative sampling. The proposed architecture separates the generation of candidate negative pools, conditioned on an explicit context, from the selection strategy, enabling the development and integration of static, schema-aware and dynamic approaches within a consistent framework. Based on this abstraction, we implement six negative samplers, while remaining fully compatible with existing PyKEEN workflows and pipelines. As a proof of concept, we study negative availability across four datasets, showing that constrained pools frequently fall below the requested number of negatives, so that the encoded criterion is to a large extent replaced by the random fallback that supplements them.

title: SIR: Self-improving Red-teaming for Compute Use Agents
abstract: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are agents powered by vision-language models (VLMs) that perceive a screen and operate an operating system through mouse, keyboard, and terminal interactions to automate everyday digital tasks. Their exposure to untrusted content creates a risk of indirect prompt injection (IPI), where an adversary embeds instructions in content the agent reads to redirect it toward actions that violate the user's intent. Evaluations based on fixed, hand-written injections may underestimate the risk posed by adaptive adversaries. We present SIR, a black-box self-improving IPI framework that (i) composes task-specific injections from a small library of reusable red-teaming principles stated in plain language and (ii) uses an iterative feedback loop to analyze unsuccessful attack trajectories and distill new, named principles that are retained in a shared library and reused across tasks. We target operating-system-level compromise and evaluate outcomes through deterministic checks on filesystem, service, and permission state rather than an LLM judge. An attack counts as successful only when both the adversarial objective and the benign user task are completed in the same execution. We evaluate three frontier CUAs, allowing SIR up to 10 attack attempts per case. It achieves joint attack success rates of 24% on Claude Opus 4.8 and 28% on Gemini 3.5 Flash, compared with 4% and 0%, respectively, for the benchmark's fixed, hand-written injection. The red-teaming principles discovered against one victim also improve attacks against other victims, including a different model family, without additional feedback.

title: Research on Neural Network Technology in Public Safety Anomaly and Hazard Detection
abstract: Abnormal hazards in public places have the characteristics of low frequency, diversity and strong timeliness. Single video model is easily affected by occlusion, illumination and network interruption. In this article, an abnormal danger detection method is constructed, which combines the temporal and spatial characteristics of video, environmental sensing information and communication status, and introduces the neural network synchronization control mechanism under DoS attack. The model uses convolutional network to extract local appearance and motion information, describes the evolution of events with gated time series units, and then completes multi-source feature fusion through attention mechanism. When DoS attacks cause intermittent loss of node data, state observation and synchronization compensation are introduced to maintain the time consistency between the edge detection results and the central model. The experimental results show that the F1 value of the proposed method reaches 0.922, which remains at 0.861 under the packet loss rate of 40%. Synchronous compensation reduces the average state error by about 41.7%. The research shows that the combination of dangerous content identification and network operation state can improve the stability of public safety anomaly detection under the condition of disturbed communication.

title: Ethical use of AI in E-commerce Product recommendations- Consumer trust in Shopsy
abstract: Abstract AI has been a significant influence in the Indian e-commerce landscape, particularly on social commerce sites such as Shopsy, where AI algorithms are capable of creating product suggestions that drive sales. These suggestions make shopping simpler, more applicable and also boost sales. They also pose some significant questions. Is there merit in the suggestions? Is user data safe? Do people understand the purpose of the product(s) they are seeing? But have you ever felt like recommendations were too personal? This is even more crucial for Shopsy, given the reseller-based business model. In this case, there are two levels of trust: between the platform and the reseller; between the reseller and the customer. In the event an AI suggestion is not ethical, trust can fall at both levels and impact the entire business. The study focuses on the ethical use of AI in product recommendations, consumer trust, effects on consumer purchase intention and customer loyalty on Shopsy. The focus is on three ethical aspects: transparency, fairness, and data privacy. The study also examines whether the ttrust decreases when the respondents feel that recommendations are “too intrusive.” For that purpose, Primary data were collected from 50 active Shopsy users and resellers in tier-1, tier-2 and tier-3 cities in India. This was an instrument that consisted of a structured Google Form questionnaire with a 5-point Likert scale. It has been investigated three hypotheses: 1) the relationship between ethical AI and consumer trust; 2) the relationship between consumer trust and purchase intention and loyalty; and 3) the moderator of perceived intrusiveness. Existing literature indicates that transparency, fairness, and privacy are important factors in establishing trust. Users will be more likely to purchase and remain loyal when they have confidence in the ethics and non-intrusiveness of the AI. However, excessive personalisation or lack of control can lead to a loss of trust. This insight prompts important recommendations for Shopsy, such as making recommendations explainable, conducting bias audits, providing data control options, adhering to the DPDP Act 2023, and educating resellers on responsible usage of AI. The research fills a gap in Indian social-commerce and offers a straightforward structure that strikes a balance between personalization and ethics, fostering sustainable growth. The terms used in the article are featured in bold and underlined. The article uses the following keywords, which are bold and underlined. Artificial Intelligence (AI), E-commerce, Product Recommendation, Consumer Trust, Shopsy

title: Wallhacks, Bots, and the Arms Race: A Narrative Review of Anti-Cheat and Security in Online Games
abstract: Online games are adversarial distributed systems twice over: the design pits players against players, and the security pits every player against the cheaters who modify clients, automate play, and exploit the network. This article presents a narrative review of the literature of that arms race. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the cheat taxonomy, in which Yan and Randell's systematic classification, Hoglund and McCamish's exploitation anatomy, Webb and Soh's survey, and Consalvo's sociological study fixed the enemy's catalog --- modified clients, automation, information exploits, and the social worlds of gaining advantage; the detection systems, in which Yeung's statistical cheater detection, Pao's avatar-trajectory analysis, Thawonmas's behavioral bot detection, and Mitterhofer's server-side techniques fixed the server's counters --- machine learning over movement, the bot's statistical shadow, and the client's integrity checks; and the security frame, in which Anderson's security engineering, the zero-day economics of Bilge and Dumitras, the botnet takeovers of Stone-Gross and colleagues, and the software-exploitation tradition of Hoglund and McGraw placed game security in the discipline's larger war. It is concluded that the literature describes an arms race with a moving frontier: every detection layer (statistical, behavioral, kernel-level) escalates the attacker's layer (client mods, bots, drivers), and the field's settled wisdom is architectural --- cheat resistance designed into the protocol beats cheat detection bolted onto the client.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Topological Structure Analysis and Computation
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, exhibits unique properties that challenge classical intuition. This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement to manifest within non-linear topological structures, exploring novel quantum computation models based on this principle. We propose a framework that leverages the inherent topological properties of quantum states, aiming to enhance entanglement stability and computational efficiency. The core mechanism focuses on optimizing quantum circuit topology to mitigate entanglement decoherence, a persistent challenge in quantum information processing. The research explores the impact of topological structure on quantum entanglement, providing a novel approach to improve the performance of quantum algorithms. This work offers a new perspective on harnessing quantum entanglement for advanced computational applications, potentially revolutionizing the landscape of quantum information theory.

title: Probability Logic and Quantum Information Fusion
abstract: This paper explores the synergistic integration of probability logic and set theory, aiming to construct a novel probabilistic framework capable of efficiently storing, transmitting, and processing quantum information. The core mechanism involves the fusion of the probabilistic properties inherent in probability logic with the abstract nature of set theory, leveraging these properties to enable quantum information manipulation. This work proposes a new approach to quantum information processing, addressing limitations of existing techniques and offering a potential pathway towards advanced quantum computing and communication.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Dynamic Routing of Distributed Computing Resources
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to dynamic routing in distributed computing systems leveraging the phenomenon of quantum entanglement. Traditional routing algorithms suffer from latency issues inherent in classical networks, limiting their efficiency and scalability. Our approach utilizes entangled nodes to provide instantaneous information about the state of the entire distributed network, enabling real-time awareness and optimized routing decisions. We introduce a framework where each computing node is entangled with a designated "entanglement node." Measurements of the entanglement node's quantum state provide immediate information about the states of all connected computing nodes. Routing decisions are then based on probability distributions derived from these entangled states, further optimized using quantum algorithms. This method offers a significant reduction in routing latency and promises a more efficient and scalable distributed computing architecture. The core claim of this work is that quantum entanglement can enable significantly more efficient and faster dynamic routing, overcoming the bottlenecks present in classical network routing. ---

title: Causal Discovery Based on Multi-Variable Probabilistic Models
abstract: This paper explores the application of multi-variable probabilistic models for causal discovery. Traditional causal discovery methods often rely heavily on domain expertise and observational data, presenting significant challenges in complex systems where such information is limited or unavailable. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing multi-variable probabilistic models, specifically Bayesian Networks and Structural Causal Models, to automatically learn and infer causal relationships. The core mechanism involves employing algorithms designed for probabilistic inference within these models. The resulting framework offers a data-driven method for identifying causal connections, potentially reducing the reliance on pre-existing knowledge and facilitating discovery in scenarios with sparse or incomplete information. We demonstrate the theoretical underpinnings of this approach and outline a methodology for its implementation, focusing on the ability to model complex dependencies and ultimately, uncover underlying causal structures. This work contributes to a more automated and robust approach to causal inference, opening up possibilities for analysis in diverse fields. ---

title: Relational Causal Inference via Differential Privacy
abstract: Causal inference from observational data is a critical challenge in numerous domains, yet it's notoriously susceptible to biases arising from confounding variables and selection effects. Simultaneously, the increasing availability of sensitive data necessitates robust privacy protection mechanisms. This research proposes a novel framework for relational causal inference that integrates differential privacy (DP) directly into the causal discovery and effect estimation processes. The core idea leverages graphical models – specifically, Bayesian networks – to represent causal relationships, combined with DP algorithms designed to mitigate the risk of information leakage while maintaining the accuracy of causal effect estimates. We introduce a new approach to incorporating DP constraints during the structure learning phase of Bayesian networks, addressing a significant gap in existing DP-based causal inference methods. The framework's theoretical properties are explored, demonstrating the potential for achieving both strong causal inference capabilities and rigorous privacy guarantees. We outline a methodology for quantifying the trade-off between privacy parameters (ε, δ) and the accuracy of causal effect estimation, offering guidance for practical implementation. This work represents a significant step forward in enabling reliable and privacy-conscious causal discovery in real-world scenarios.

abstract: This paper explores the application of multi-scale cognitive graphs for knowledge discovery. The core claim is that constructing such graphs, representing knowledge at varying granularities, allows for a more nuanced understanding of complex systems and facilitates more effective knowledge extraction. The proposed mechanism involves mapping knowledge into multi-scale graphs, utilizing graph analysis algorithms – including node discovery, pathfinding, and pattern recognition – to unveil patterns and relationships. This approach moves beyond the limitations of traditional knowledge graphs that often operate at a single scale. The research demonstrates the potential of multi-scale graphs to provide a more holistic and insightful representation of complex systems, leading to novel knowledge generation. The resulting graph structures are analyzed to identify emergent relationships and patterns, ultimately contributing to a deeper understanding of the system under investigation. The key contribution lies in the systematic framework for constructing and analyzing these multi-scale graphs, offering a robust method for knowledge discovery in complex domains. ---
