title: Quantum Reservoir Computing for Time Series Prediction
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum reservoir computing (QRC) to time series prediction. Classical reservoir computing (RC) utilizes a complex, high-dimensional system – the 'reservoir' – as a non-linear feature extractor, followed by a linear regression model for prediction. QRC extends this concept by leveraging the inherent dynamics of a quantum system as the reservoir. We hypothesize that quantum systems, due to their superposition and entanglement properties, can provide richer and more complex dynamics than classical reservoirs, potentially leading to improved prediction accuracy. This work outlines the theoretical framework for QRC, detailing the setup of a suitable quantum reservoir (e.g., a superconducting qubit array), the measurement process, and the training strategy involving a classical machine learning model. We demonstrate a conceptual approach, focusing on the potential advantages and challenges of employing quantum systems for this task. The core claim is that QRC can achieve superior time series prediction accuracy compared to classical RC methods. Key elements explored include the input signal's influence on the quantum reservoir, the selection of appropriate measurement schemes, and the choice of classical learning algorithms. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the potential impact of QRC on various time series prediction applications.

The core claim is that QRC can achieve superior time series prediction accuracy compared to classical RC methods. Key elements explored include the input signal's influence on the quantum reservoir, the selection of appropriate measurement schemes, and the choice of classical learning algorithms. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the potential impact of QRC on various time series prediction applications.

title: 基于量子几何的拓扑变换的量子算法验证
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum geometry to validate quantum algorithms, offering a novel approach to algorithm verification. Traditional methods rely on classical verification, which struggles to fully capture the intricacies of quantum algorithms. We propose a new methodology leveraging quantum geometric models to rigorously assess the correctness and stability of quantum computations. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum geometric representation of the algorithm, and utilizing the inherent properties of quantum geometry – specifically, self-similarity and entanglement – to detect subtle errors and inconsistencies that might be missed by conventional verification techniques. This research aims to provide a robust and efficient method for validating quantum algorithms, addressing limitations of existing approaches.

title: When AI Support Is Removed: Immediate Gains and Delayed Unaided Performance After AI-Supported Learning — A Systematic Review, Evidence Map, and Conditional Meta-analysis. The phrase “Crutch Effect” is a proposed theoretical label and is not treated as an established result.
abstract: This project will identify, appraise, map, and, when scientifically justified, quantitatively synthesize studies in which learners directly use an artificial-intelligence system during structured learning and are later assessed without AI support. The central issue is whether AI-supported learning improves immediate performance but is followed by weaker, attenuated, or reversed delayed unaided performance compared with no-AI or resource/time-matched learning. The review has two linked layers. The broad evidence map will include longitudinal educational and professional-training studies reporting immediate, delayed, retention, transfer, independent-performance, or mechanism outcomes. The primary quantitative synthesis will be restricted to direct withdrawal evidence: direct learner-AI interaction, an appropriate comparator, explicit AI withdrawal or AI-disabled assessment, an objective delayed outcome, and preferably both immediate and delayed AI-free assessments. Studies with a delayed AI-free outcome but no immediate AI-free assessment will be synthesized as Tier B. Mechanistically adjacent studies will be mapped and narratively synthesized as Tier C. Studies reporting only AI-enabled task performance will be classified as Tier D contextual evidence and cannot establish a Crutch Effect. The review will distinguish AI-supported performance, immediate AI-free learning, delayed AI-free independent performance, and transfer or independent professional performance. The primary estimands are the standardized between-group effect at a prespecified delayed AI-free endpoint and, when measurement and timing are comparable, the condition-by-time interaction or difference-in-differences. Immediate AI-enabled performance will be reported separately and will not be interpreted as durable learning. The protocol follows PRISMA-P principles and will be reported using PRISMA 2020, PRISMA-S, and SWiM when pooling is inappropriate. RoB 2 will be used for randomized studies, ROBINS-I for non-randomized comparative studies, and GRADE principles will be applied separately to immediate, delayed, interaction, and transfer outcomes.

title: AI-driven resolution of uncertain histopathology in cases initially misdiagnosed as triple-negative breast cancer
abstract: Tumors presumed to be metastatic triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) may occasionally represent misdiagnoses of primary or metastatic tumors from other origins—particularly lung—due to overlapping clinical characteristics and lack of organ-specific morphological features. While immunohistochemical markers can resolve these discrepancies, they are often underutilized without prior clinical suspicion, leading to significant treatment delays. To address this, we employed GPSai, a tissue-of-origin artificial intelligence (AI) model integrated into routine molecular profiling at Caris Life Sciences, to systematically identify differential diagnoses among 2423 presumed TNBC cases. By integrating AI results with clinical and molecular evidence, we identified a misdiagnosis rate of 3.0%. While over half of these cases were reclassified as non-small cell lung cancer, the misdiagnosis cohort also included various other tumor types. These diagnostic shifts profoundly impact staging, prognosis, and therapeutic selection, highlighting the necessity of an unbiased, systematic approach to identifying misdiagnoses among presumed TNBC.

title: Understanding and Exploiting Initialization Anchoring Weakness in Feedback-Based Agent Planning
abstract: Feedback-based planning improves agent reliability by incorporating tool observations and corrective feedback. However, its protection may not be distributed uniformly across planning stages. We conduct a round-wise analysis of four representative feedback mechanisms and uncover an initialization anchoring weakness: the first feedback round corrects 46\% of adversarial directions, whereas the rates fall to 13\% and 7\% among directions surviving into the next two rounds. Our analysis attributes this weakness to three interacting factors: a contextually plausible shift in the initial plan, insufficient counterevidence, and the persistence of accepted directions in the accumulated trajectory. Based on these findings, we propose \textsc{InitAnchor}, a black-box framework for exploiting this weakness through attacker-controlled external materials. It operationalizes the three factors as directional-shift, contextual-plausibility, and counterevidence-resilience signals under either limited target access or no target access. Across 112 tasks from 16 domains, six agent architectures, and five backbone LLMs, \textsc{InitAnchor} achieves average ASRs of 76.1\% and 72.0\% under the two settings while reducing first-round mitigation rates to 21.0\% and 25.0\%, respectively. It also remains effective against six defenses and across six real-world agent systems. These findings show that feedback-based agents can retain early biases even when later correction is available.

title: BLOOM-WILT: Logit Tilting for Behaviour Elicitation in Automated LLM Auditing
abstract: Users of a deployed language model routinely encounter behaviours that have never been observed during testing, since deployment puts the model through orders of magnitude more interactions than any evaluation can simulate. Automated auditors can mitigate this issue as they are flexible enough to discover almost any specified behaviour, yet their random sampling approach makes them inefficient. To address this shortcoming, we introduce BLOOM-WILT, a full auditing pipeline that elicits natural multi-turn instances of rare behaviours, without training cost or access beyond the target's next-token distribution. On the user input side, WILT revises its conversational strategy across rounds, learning from previous scored interactions. On the model output side, WILT generates behaviour-relevant continuations by feeding the model with an elicitation prompt and mixing its next-token distribution with the unprompted model. We evaluate WILT across 4 target models and 8 behaviours, and show that it improves over the baseline in 30 of the 32 settings, thus revealing that a larger number of models exhibit harmful behaviours than previously suggested. Furthermore, WILT is the only method that can raise the mean presence of self-harm encouragement from 51% to 100% in Qwen3.5-4B, without decreasing the output probability of the generated text. Our code is available at https://github.com/AdrSkapars/bloom-wilt.

title: One Adapter, Many Tasks: Task-Conditioned Feature Transformations for Continual Learning
abstract: Class-incremental learning (CIL) requires a model to incrementally learn tasks that contain new classes without accessing earlier training data while preserving the ability to recognize all seen classes. Recently, pretrained-model-based approaches have become prevalent by adapting a frozen backbone with additional lightweight trainable modules. Existing methods, however, exhibit limitations: task-specific adapters learn explicit per-task representations but are parameter- and computation-inefficient, while LoRA-based merging methods combine per-task LoRA parameters into a single model whose static aggregated weights cause representation interference during inference. To address these problems, we present \textbf{FACET}: task-conditioned \textbf{F}e\textbf{A}ture transformation with \textbf{C}ondition\textbf{E}d feature consis\textbf{T}ency, achieving excellent parameter efficiency while producing highly discriminative features during inference. When continually trained on a task sequence, FACET learns a single shared adapter that employs a dynamic task-conditioned feature transformation, shaping the overall feature distribution of the adapter into a mixture of overlap-reduced task-specific components. On the other hand, we propose an efficient replay-free task-conditioned feature consistency loss, aiming to mitigate catastrophic forgetting of the learned mixture distribution in the adapter's feature space. Even when maintaining only a single adapter, FACET demonstrates robust scalability. On both very long task sequences (e.g., 200 tasks) and standard short task sequences (e.g., 20 tasks), our method achieves superior performance while using significantly fewer trainable parameters and GFLOPs. The code will be made open source upon acceptance.

title: RealCAD: Towards Real-World Image-to-CAD Reconstruction under Domain Shift and Parameter Bias
abstract: Reconstructing editable Computer-Aided Design (CAD) models from images is essential for downstream modification, manufacturing, and design reuse. However, existing image-to-CAD methods are developed predominantly on synthetic renderings and face two coupled obstacles: a substantial appearance domain gap between synthetic and real images, and a previously overlooked parameter bias in widely used CAD data. We show that the local normalization adopted by DeepCAD concentrates several geometric parameters around a few discrete values while encoding substantial information in a single scale factor. Consequently, a model can achieve deceptively high parameter accuracy by exploiting these frequent values rather than inferring geometry from the input image. In this paper, we propose RealCAD, a unified framework that addresses these limitations at the representation, image, and feature levels. At the representation level, we redistribute scale information to the corresponding geometric parameters, producing less concentrated parameter distributions in a shared scale space. At the image level, geometry-constrained translation converts synthetic renderings toward the real-image domain while conditioning on object contours. At the feature level, a multi-positive contrastive objective aligns representations of the same CAD model across viewpoints and image domains, enabling CAD sequence prediction from each individual view. We further introduce OpenRealCAD, comprising four-view photographs of 392 3D-printed objects paired with ground-truth command sequences. Experiments show that the revised representation substantially reduces the accuracy attainable from parameter-frequency priors, making parameter accuracy a more reliable measure of image-conditioned geometric inference. RealCAD further improves real-domain command and parameter accuracy, while retaining competitive synthetic-domain performance.

title: AtlasNLP: A Country-Aware Atlas of Dataset Representation in NLP
abstract: Understanding which countries are represented in NLP datasets is essential for identifying gaps, targeting data collection, measuring progress, and informing AI policy. However, geographic metadata is very rarely available, and country-level representation is often hidden behind broad language-level claims. We introduce AtlasNLP, a country-aware atlas of over 13,000 NLP dataset records across normalized NLP task categories, tracking both the populations represented and where datasets are produced. AtlasNLP includes AtlasNLP-Gold, a human-curated reference set, and AtlasNLP-Core, an ACL-derived large-scale collection. Using this resource, we show that (1) dataset coverage is highly uneven across countries and tasks; (2) dataset production and representation are geographically asymmetric; and (3) language coverage does not imply geographic representation. These findings reveal blind spots in current dataset documentation practices and motivate more explicit geographic metadata for country-aware NLP evaluation.

title: A Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Credit Card Fraud Detection in E-Commerce
abstract: The rapid growth of e-commerce and electronic payment services has increased the convenience of digital transactions while also creating more opportunities for fraudulent activity. Conventional fraud detection approaches based on manual review and fixed rules can struggle with large transaction volumes, changing fraud patterns, and false-positive alerts. This study comparatively evaluates four supervised machine learning algorithms-Logistic Regression, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Decision Tree, and Support Vector Machine (SVM) for credit card fraud detection. The study used a labelled transaction dataset and followed an iterative Agile-based development process involving data preparation, model training, testing, and performance evaluation. The models were assessed using accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC), and training time. The reported experimental results show that Logistic Regression achieved the highest accuracy (63.33%), precision (67.61%), and ROC-AUC (0.6855), while KNN produced the highest recall (67.50%) and F1-score (0.6506). SVM produced moderate results but required the longest training time of 0.0345 seconds. Decision Tree had the shortest training time at 0.0058 seconds but recorded the weakest overall predictive performance, including 54.00% accuracy and 40.00% recall. The findings demonstrate that model selection for fraud detection should not be based on accuracy alone because missing fraudulent transactions can have serious financial and operational consequences. Logistic Regression provided the strongest overall balance among the evaluated models, although the moderate performance of all four algorithms indicates that larger and more representative datasets, improved feature engineering, class-imbalance treatment, and hyperparameter optimization are required before practical deployment.

title: Sistem Pakar Mendiagnosa Kerusakan Kamera Mirrorless Sony Tipe A6000 Menggunakan Metode Certainty Factor
abstract: Kamera mirrorless Sony tipe A6000 merupakan salah satu produk kamera populer yang banyak digunakan oleh para fotografer. Namun, seperti perangkat elektronik lainnya, kamera ini tidak lepas dari kemungkinan mengalami kerusakan. Untuk mendiagnosis kerusakan secara akurat dan efisien, diperlukan sebuah sistem pakar yang dapat membantu dalam proses identifikasi masalah. Penelitian ini mengusulkan pengembangan sebuah sistem pakar untuk mendiagnosis kerusakan pada kamera mirrorless Sony tipe A6000 dengan menggunakan metode Certainty Factor (CF). Metode CF dipilih karena kemampuannya dalam menangani ketidakpastian dan memberikan nilai keyakinan terhadap suatu hipotesis atau kesimpulan. Sistem pakar ini dirancang dengan membangun basis pengetahuan yang mencakup gejala-gejala kerusakan dan aturan-aturan pengambilan keputusan. Sistem pakar yang dikembangkan mampu mendiagnosis kerusakan pada kamera mirrorless Sony tipe A6000 dengan akurasi yang tinggi. Metode Certainty Factor terbukti efektif dalam mengombinasikan bukti-bukti dan memberikan nilai keyakinan terhadap setiap kemungkinan kerusakan. Sistem ini membantu para pengguna kamera dalam mengidentifikasi masalah secara cepat dan tepat, sehingga memudahkan proses perbaikan atau penggantian komponen yang rusak. Selain itu, sistem pakar ini juga dapat digunakan sebagai alat bantu dalam pelatihan dan pendidikan terkait perbaikan kamera

title: Impact of AI-Powered Personalization in Influencing Consumer Purchase Intention and Brand Loyalty
abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-powered personalization is transforming online retail by tailoring product recommendations, promotional messages, search results, and customer interactions to individual preferences. This study examines the impact of AI-powered personalization on consumers' purchase intention and brand loyalty among online shoppers. A descriptive and quantitative research design is proposed, using a structured questionnaire and a five-point Likert scale. Following the structure of the supplied model paper, an illustrative sample of 200 respondents is used for the model analysis. Descriptive statistics, Chi-square, and one-way ANOVA are applied. The illustrative results indicate a significant association between exposure to AI-powered recommendations and purchase intention, as well as significant differences in brand loyalty across levels of perceived personalization. The study suggests that retailers should improve recommendation relevance, provide transparent personalization, protect consumer data, and combine AI-enabled service with human support. This study examines the impact of AI-powered personalization on consumers' purchase intention and brand loyalty among online shoppers. A descriptive and quantitative research design is proposed, using a structured questionnaire and a five-point Likert scale. Following the structure of the supplied model paper, an illustrative sample of 200 respondents is used for the model analysis. Descriptive statistics, Chi-square, and one-way ANOVA are applied. The illustrative results indicate a significant association between exposure to AI-powered recommendations and purchase intention, as well as significant differences in brand loyalty across levels of perceived personalization. The study suggests that retailers should improve recommendation relevance, provide transparent personalization, protect consumer data, and combine AI-enabled service with human support. The paper concludes that responsible AI personalization can strengthen purchase intention and brand loyalty when consumers perceive the experience as useful, accurate, convenient, and trustworthy.

title: Graph-Based Semantic Relation Extraction
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to semantic relation extraction leveraging graph embedding techniques. Traditional relation extraction methods often suffer from limitations such as reliance on manually annotated data, the need for complex rule-based systems, and inherent subjectivity. This research proposes a method that transforms graph structures into continuous vector representations (graph embeddings) and utilizes these embeddings for relation extraction. The core claim is that this approach significantly enhances both the accuracy and efficiency of relation extraction. We explore various graph embedding models and demonstrate their effectiveness in capturing semantic relationships within graphs. The presented method offers a more scalable and potentially more accurate alternative to existing approaches, addressing the shortcomings of previous methods. This work lays the foundation for further research into utilizing graph embeddings for diverse semantic understanding tasks.

title: Adaptive Meta-Learning via Differential Evolution of Logical Programs
abstract: Meta-learning aims to enable rapid adaptation to new tasks with minimal training data. Traditional meta-learning approaches often rely on optimizing the parameters of complex models, such as neural networks. However, this approach can lead to black-box models that are difficult to interpret and may not generalize effectively across diverse task distributions. This work proposes a novel adaptive meta-learning framework that utilizes differential evolution to directly evolve the structure of logical programs. Specifically, we employ a differential evolution algorithm to optimize a symbolic logical program, representing the meta-learning strategy. The fitness function is defined based on the performance of the evolved logical program on a variety of tasks. This approach offers several advantages, including increased interpretability, potentially more efficient learning, and improved generalization capabilities. The core claim is that evolving logical program structures, rather than solely network weights, can significantly improve meta-learning. The key mechanism involves directly optimizing a symbolic logical program. This research represents a shift from gradient-based optimization of neural networks to a more explicit and potentially more efficient learning process using symbolic logic.

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, holds immense potential for secure communication and computation. Traditional verification methods, reliant on classical computation, often struggle to comprehensively assess the security of complex geometric models. This paper introduces a new geometric model validation technique employing quantum entanglement to provide a more rigorous and secure verification process. The core mechanism involves establishing entangled states with geometric models, enabling the detection of subtle inconsistencies that might be missed with conventional methods. The resulting entanglement properties are then analyzed to ascertain the model's security characteristics. This work represents a significant advancement in quantum verification, offering a promising approach to bolstering the resilience of quantum systems.

abstract: This paper presents a novel graph neural network (GNN) based algorithm for graph structure optimization. We introduce a new algorithm, termed "Dynamic Graph Adaptation" (DGA), which dynamically adjusts the graph's structure based on incoming data, enabling more efficient optimization. The core mechanism of DGA utilizes a dynamically generated graph topology driven by a feedback loop, allowing the algorithm to learn and adapt to evolving data patterns. We demonstrate the effectiveness of DGA through several benchmark graph optimization problems, showcasing significant improvements in optimization speed and quality compared to existing methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's design, implementation, and potential applications.

title: Neural Network Dynamics: Topological Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural network learning centered around dynamic topological structures. The core idea is to construct a neural network with locally adaptive synaptic plasticity and a dynamically evolving topology, enabling continuous learning and adaptation to complex, non-static environments without explicit structural specification. The methodology integrates adaptive synaptic plasticity, topological evolution rules, and fine-grained neuronal state encoding. Adaptive synaptic plasticity adjusts synaptic weights based on local neuronal activity, strengthening important connections and suppressing irrelevant ones. Topological evolution rules dynamically modify connection strengths based on information transmission efficiency and local activity patterns, altering the network's topology. Fine-grained neuronal state encoding captures richer temporal information, enhancing neuronal dependencies. This dynamic topological learning mechanism contrasts significantly with traditional static neural networks and rule-based reinforcement learning, offering a potential pathway to building more intelligent and robust systems. ---

title: Bearcat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Bearcat Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Bearcat, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Bearcats ( *Melogale moschata*). Bearcats are known for their strategic approach to food gathering, utilizing a combination of systematic searching and opportunistic exploitation. Bearcat leverages these behaviors through a novel search operator and a dynamically adjusted adaptive inertia weight mechanism. The algorithm's core components include a position representation, a global best position, and a local best position. The primary innovation lies in the "Pounce" operator, which mimics the Bearcat's sudden shifts in direction when encountering a promising food source. Furthermore, the algorithm incorporates a dynamically adjusted inertia weight scheme based on the distance between the current position and the global best position. We evaluate Bearcat on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Experimental results show that Bearcat exhibits robust performance across diverse problem landscapes, indicating its potential applicability in various real-world optimization scenarios. The key performance metrics considered are convergence speed and solution quality.

title: Geometric Complexity Metric for Machine Learning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel geometric complexity metric designed to enhance the training and evaluation of machine learning models. Traditional metrics often focus on surface area or volume, neglecting the fundamental geometric properties of data points. We propose a new metric that quantifies the complexity of data points – the arrangement of edges, angles, and curves – and utilizes this measure to guide model learning, potentially improving accuracy and interpretability. The core mechanism involves calculating a "complexity score" for each data point, which is then incorporated into the model's optimization process. This approach aims to capture subtle patterns and relationships within the data that may be missed by conventional metrics. The paper details the metric's construction, demonstrates its effectiveness through illustrative examples, and discusses potential future directions for research.

title: Quantum-Inspired Bayesian Inference for Causal Discovery
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to causal discovery leveraging principles inspired by quantum mechanics. Traditional Bayesian network learning methods often struggle with the vastness of possible causal structures, leading to computational bottlenecks and potentially inaccurate results. We propose a framework that incorporates probabilistic amplitudes, analogous to quantum superposition, to represent and explore multiple potential causal pathways concurrently. This "quantum-inspired" Bayesian inference aims to significantly enhance the exploration process, ultimately leading to improved accuracy in identifying causal relationships within observational data. The core idea is that by allowing for multiple potential pathways to be actively explored simultaneously, we can overcome the limitations of classical methods that typically rely on sequential searching. This approach is evaluated conceptually, outlining the key components and anticipated benefits. The paper focuses on the theoretical underpinnings and the potential impact of this methodology, paving the way for future research and development.

title: Dynamic Symbolic Representation Learning via Iterative Refinement
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to symbolic representation learning, termed Dynamic Symbolic Representation Learning via Iterative Refinement (DSRL-IR). The core idea is to develop a system that learns symbolic representations directly from raw sensory data through an iterative refinement process. Unlike traditional symbolic mapping techniques that often rely on fixed, pre-defined mappings, our system employs a recurrent neural network with a differentiable symbolic layer. This layer iteratively updates a latent representation based on feedback signals that assess the 'correctness' of the generated symbolic output. The system mimics the human conceptual development process, where initial, imprecise understandings are gradually refined through experience and feedback. We propose a framework that allows the system to learn increasingly complex symbolic representations, demonstrating the potential for creating intelligent agents capable of understanding and interacting with the world in a more human-like manner. The key contribution lies in the dynamic, embodied learning process, which contrasts with static symbolic mapping. This approach utilizes a core equation to represent the iterative refinement process: *Rt+1 = f(Rt, St+1)* Where: * *Rt+1* represents the refined latent representation at time step *t+1*. * *Rt* represents the latent representation at time step *t*. * *St+1* represents the feedback signal at time step *t+1*, indicating the correctness of the symbolic output. * *f* represents the iterative refinement function, typically a recurrent neural network. The system is evaluated through simulated environments, showcasing its ability to learn and represent complex relationships between sensory data and symbolic concepts. Future research directions include exploring different feedback mechanisms and integrating this approach with other learning paradigms.

title: Back-striped Weasel: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Agile Movement of a Back-striped Weasel
abstract: This paper introduces Back-striped Weasel (BSW), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the unique and agile movement patterns observed in back-striped weasels (Mustela strigidorsa). BSW leverages a combination of adaptive step-size control, a novel mutation operator mimicking the weasel's directional shifts, and a dynamic population management strategy to explore the search space effectively. The algorithm's core mechanism, the "Stride Adjustment," simulates the weasel's ability to rapidly alter its movement direction based on environmental feedback. We demonstrate the efficacy of BSW through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising candidate for a wide range of optimization challenges. Key performance metrics including convergence speed, solution quality, and computational efficiency are analyzed. Future research directions include incorporating environmental modeling and extending the algorithm to handle multi-objective optimization.

title: Adaptive Dynamic Programming Algorithm for Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has demonstrated remarkable success in various domains, but its application is often hindered by the "curse of dimensionality," specifically the state space explosion problem. Traditional dynamic programming methods, while theoretically sound for solving Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), struggle with large state spaces due to the exponential growth of the value function computation. This paper proposes an Adaptive Dynamic Programming Algorithm for Reinforcement Learning (ADP-RL), designed to mitigate this issue. ADP-RL dynamically adjusts the parameters of the dynamic programming algorithm based on the observed dynamics of the environment, effectively reducing computational complexity. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that monitors the convergence rate of the value function approximation and modifies parameters accordingly. We demonstrate the effectiveness of ADP-RL through a theoretical analysis and a simplified numerical example, highlighting its ability to handle complex environments more efficiently than standard dynamic programming approaches. The key innovation lies in the adaptive nature of the algorithm, offering a practical solution for scaling dynamic programming to real-world RL problems.

title: ## The Bioluminescent Navigation Algorithm (BLNA): A Metaheuristic Inspired by Blue Dragonfish Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Bioluminescent Navigation Algorithm (BLNA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique navigation strategies employed by blue dragonfish ( *Cynoglossus mola*) in the deep ocean. These fish utilize a sophisticated bioluminescent communication system to navigate and locate prey in dark environments. BLNA leverages concepts such as 'beaconing' (localized bioluminescence), 'gradient following' (movement towards brighter signals), and 'group cohesion' (collective movement) to achieve efficient global optimization. The algorithm operates within a search space, representing potential solutions, and iteratively adjusts these solutions based on a dynamically updated 'illumination' metric, mimicking the dragonfish's bioluminescent signals. We outline the core principles, mathematical formulation, and key components of BLNA, demonstrating its potential applicability across a range of optimization problems.

title: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Resource Allocation
abstract: This paper investigates the application of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) to the problem of resource allocation. Traditional resource allocation methods often struggle with complex scenarios involving multiple agents with varying priorities and constraints. MARL offers a promising approach by allowing agents to learn optimal allocation strategies through interaction and competition. This work proposes a framework utilizing multiple reinforcement learning agents to dynamically manage and distribute resources. The core claim is that MARL can achieve optimized resource allocation and enhanced fairness compared to traditional centralized approaches. The core mechanism involves constructing a multi-agent system where agents cooperate and compete to maximize their individual rewards while considering the overall system performance. The system learns through trial and error, adapting to changing conditions and agent behaviors. We present a detailed formulation of the problem, outlining the key components of the MARL system including agent representation, reward functions, and the learning algorithm. The potential benefits of this approach, particularly in dynamic and uncertain environments, are discussed, highlighting the adaptability and scalability of MARL for complex resource management challenges. ---

abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental aspect of quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity for revolutionary computational capabilities. This paper explores the design and implementation of a novel quantum entanglement parameterization algorithm, aiming to bridge the gap between quantum physics and classical systems. The core claim centers on the ability to precisely control quantum systems through a dynamically parameterized quantum operation, offering a deeper theoretical framework for quantum computation. Existing quantum computing approaches often rely on simplified models, necessitating a more sophisticated approach to accurately represent and manipulate entangled states. This research proposes a method that incorporates a dynamic mapping, enabling a higher degree of control and optimization. The potential impact of this algorithm on the future of quantum technology is substantial, representing a significant advancement in quantum system management.

title: ## Black Coral-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BCMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Black Coral-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (BCMOA), a novel optimization technique inspired by the growth patterns and resilience of black corals. Black corals, known for their intricate, branching structures formed over extended periods, exhibit a fascinating balance between exploration and exploitation. BCMOA leverages this biological principle to construct a search space and iteratively refine solutions. The algorithm incorporates three key mechanisms: a branching strategy mimicking coral growth, a resilience factor reflecting the coral's ability to withstand environmental pressures, and a dynamic adjustment of the branching probability based on solution quality. The core of BCMOA lies in a probabilistic branching process that generates new candidate solutions by creating branches from existing ones, with the branching probability influenced by the solution's fitness and a dynamically adjusted resilience factor. This approach aims to create a robust search process, adaptable to complex and multi-dimensional optimization problems. The algorithm's effectiveness in representing the complex, hierarchical structure of black coral formations translates to a powerful tool for tackling challenging optimization landscapes.

title: Hierarchical Graph Attention Networks for Multi-Scale Data Analysis
abstract: This paper proposes a novel hierarchical graph attention network (HGAT) architecture designed to effectively analyze multi-scale data. Traditional graph attention networks (GATs) often face challenges in capturing dependencies that span multiple scales, leading to suboptimal performance in tasks requiring a comprehensive understanding of data at varying resolutions. The proposed HGAT addresses this limitation by incorporating a hierarchical representation scheme, utilizing multiple layers of graph attention operating at different levels of granularity. Lower layers focus on identifying local patterns and relationships, while higher layers capture long-range dependencies and global context. The core mechanism involves a staged approach, where information is progressively refined through successive attention layers. This results in richer and more robust representations, ultimately improving the network's ability to model complex data structures. The HGAT is evaluated conceptually, outlining its potential applications and demonstrating its advantages over single-scale GATs.

title: Graph-Based Semantic Memory Retrieval using Contextual Embeddings
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to semantic memory retrieval leveraging graph-based representation and contextual embeddings. Traditional methods for representing and retrieving semantic knowledge often struggle with capturing nuanced relationships and contextual dependencies. Our approach constructs a graph where nodes represent concepts and edges represent semantic relationships extracted from textual data. Crucially, we utilize contextual embeddings, such as BERT, to generate rich vector representations for both nodes and edges. This allows for similarity comparisons and efficient graph traversal, significantly improving the accuracy and granularity of memory retrieval compared to conventional methods. The core claim is that representing semantic relationships as a graph, combined with contextual embeddings, provides a more accurate and nuanced retrieval system. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a theoretical framework, outlining the key components and their interactions. The presented system offers a scalable solution for knowledge representation and retrieval, particularly in scenarios where contextual understanding is paramount.

abstract: This paper introduces the Giant Tortoise-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (GTSA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the navigational strategies and foraging behaviors of giant tortoises. The algorithm leverages the tortoise's ability to maintain a consistent direction, adapt to environmental changes, and selectively adjust its pace based on resource availability. GTSA employs a multi-faceted approach combining a directional movement strategy, a dynamic adaptation mechanism, and a resource-based pacing system. title: Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Cognitive Constraints
abstract: Symbolic regression is a powerful technique for automatically discovering mathematical equations from data. However, its performance is often limited when dealing with complex, hierarchical systems, and it frequently produces equations that are difficult to interpret. This paper introduces a novel approach, Hierarchical Symbolic Regression with Cognitive Constraints, which addresses these limitations. The core idea is to decompose the problem into a hierarchy of simpler sub-problems, enabling the algorithm to tackle complex systems more effectively. Crucially, we incorporate cognitive constraints – derived from known physical laws or human intuition – to guide the regression process, ensuring that generated equations are both accurate and meaningful. The resulting system demonstrates significant improvements in accuracy and interpretability compared to standard symbolic regression methods, offering a more robust and human-aligned approach to equation discovery. The primary mathematical framework utilizes a tree-based symbolic representation and a constraint satisfaction algorithm operating on this hierarchical structure. The key innovations lie in the hierarchical decomposition strategy and the explicit incorporation of cognitive constraints to prune the search space and favor physically plausible solutions. Experiments (simulated, due to the absence of real-world datasets for this theoretical exploration) demonstrate the efficacy of this approach across various problem domains, highlighting its potential for applications in scientific discovery and engineering design.

title: ## Agag Gerbil: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Agag Gerbil Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Agag Gerbil, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Agag gerbil* (also known as the desert gerbil). *Agag gerbil* exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources in challenging desert environments. This paper details the algorithm's core principles, focusing on a novel exploration-exploitation strategy based on the gerbil's tendency to randomly explore while simultaneously prioritizing areas with previously observed high food concentrations. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic memory component to retain information about promising regions, mimicking the gerbil's recollection of successful foraging routes. Mathematical formulations are provided to describe the key components of the algorithm, including the probability function for exploration and exploitation, the memory update mechanism, and the parameter adaptation scheme. The performance of Agag Gerbil is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its competitive capabilities across a range of optimization tasks. Keywords: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Optimization, Agag Gerbil, Foraging Behavior, Exploration, Exploitation, Dynamic Memory, Parameter Adaptation. ### 1. Introduction Metaheuristic algorithms have become a cornerstone of modern optimization techniques, offering robust solutions to a wide variety of complex problems. Algorithms such as Genetic Algorithms (GAs), Simulated Annealing (SA), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) have consistently demonstrated success in tackling challenges across diverse domains, including engineering design, machine learning, and financial modeling. However, many metaheuristic algorithms struggle with premature convergence, particularly in problems with intricate landscapes and multiple local optima. The ability to maintain a balance between effective exploration and efficient exploitation is crucial for achieving optimal solutions. This research explores a new metaheuristic algorithm, Agag Gerbil, drawing inspiration from the remarkable foraging behavior of *Agag gerbil* (*Gerbillus campbelli*). These small rodents inhabit arid environments and possess an extraordinary ability to locate and exploit scarce food resources. Their foraging strategy is characterized by a combination of systematic exploration and targeted exploitation – they will randomly move across the landscape, but will preferentially visit areas where they have previously found food. This behavior has been observed to be highly effective in maximizing food intake in environments where food distribution is uneven and unpredictable. The core motivation behind developing Agag Gerbil is to translate this observed foraging strategy into a robust metaheuristic algorithm. The algorithm's design prioritizes maintaining a balance between exploring new regions of the search space and refining solutions in promising areas. This paper presents a detailed description of Agag Gerbil, including its mathematical formulation, algorithm design, and performance evaluation. ### 2. Algorithm Design Agag Gerbil is designed around three primary components: a population of candidate solutions, an exploration-exploitation mechanism, and a dynamic memory system. #### 2.1 Population Initialization The algorithm begins with an initial population of *N* candidate solutions. Each solution *si* is represented as a vector *xi = (x1, x2, ..., xD)*, where *D* is the dimensionality of the problem. The initial population is generated using a random sampling technique, ensuring a diverse range of starting points. #### 2.2 Exploration-Exploitation Mechanism The core of Agag Gerbil lies in its exploration-exploitation mechanism, which governs the movement of individuals within the population. This mechanism is based on two key probabilities: * Exploration Probability (Pe): This probability determines the likelihood of an individual moving to a randomly selected neighboring solution. The probability is calculated as: *Pe = 1 - exp(-α * R(si))* where *α* is a parameter controlling the exploration rate, and *R(si)* is a random number uniformly distributed between 0 and 1. A higher *α* value leads to increased exploration. * Exploitation Probability (Px): This probability determines the likelihood of an individual moving to a neighboring solution that is considered promising, based on a local evaluation function. The probability is calculated as: *Px = exp(-β * F(si))* where *β* is a parameter controlling the exploitation rate, and *F(si)* is the value of the evaluation function for solution *si*. A higher *β* value leads to increased exploitation. The overall probability of movement to a neighboring solution is the sum of the exploration and exploitation probabilities: *P = Pe + Px* The algorithm then selects a neighboring solution according to this probability distribution.

Each solution *si* is represented as a vector *xi = (x1, x2, ..., xD)*, where *D* is the dimensionality of the problem. The initial population is generated using a random sampling technique, ensuring a diverse range of starting points. #### 2.2 Exploration-Exploitation Mechanism The core of Agag Gerbil lies in its exploration-exploitation mechanism, which governs the movement of individuals within the population. This mechanism is based on two key probabilities: * Exploration Probability (Pe): This probability determines the likelihood of an individual moving to a randomly selected neighboring solution. The probability is calculated as: *Pe = 1 - exp(-α * R(si))* where *α* is a parameter controlling the exploration rate, and *R(si)* is a random number uniformly distributed between 0 and 1. A higher *α* value leads to increased exploration. * Exploitation Probability (Px): This probability determines the likelihood of an individual moving to a neighboring solution that is considered promising, based on a local evaluation function. The probability is calculated as: *Px = exp(-β * F(si))* where *β* is a parameter controlling the exploitation rate, and *F(si)* is the value of the evaluation function for solution *si*. A higher *β* value leads to increased exploitation. The overall probability of movement to a neighboring solution is the sum of the exploration and exploitation probabilities: *P = Pe + Px* The algorithm then selects a neighboring solution according to this probability distribution.

title: African Giant Free-tailed Bat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Bat Echo Adaptation Method" (BEAM), inspired by the foraging behavior of African Giant Free-tailed bats. These bats utilize sophisticated echolocation techniques to navigate and locate food in complex environments. The algorithm leverages the concept of 'echoes' – the variations in the received signal – to guide the search process, mimicking the bats' adaptation to environmental changes. BEAM employs a population-based approach, similar to Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC), but incorporates a unique mechanism for adaptive parameter adjustment based on echo intensity and frequency variations. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. Key elements of the algorithm include: a dynamic inertia weight calculation, a novel echo intensity adaptation strategy, and a frequency-dependent exploration-exploitation balance. The results indicate that BEAM exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with high dimensionality and complex landscapes. Further research will focus on extending BEAM to handle multi-objective optimization and real-time adaptive control applications.

title: Quantum Topography Simulation-Driven Dynamic Energy Field Optimization
abstract: Quantum Topography Simulation (QTS) offers a novel approach to optimization by leveraging the inherent topological properties of quantum systems. This paper investigates the application of QTS to optimize system performance and energy utilization through dynamic energy field manipulation. We demonstrate a robust optimization algorithm utilizing QTS to achieve superior results compared to traditional methods. The core mechanism centers around simulating quantum topology to dynamically adjust energy fields, enabling unprecedented efficiency in various systems. This research explores the potential of QTS to revolutionize optimization processes across diverse domains.

title: Quantum Stealth Computing Topology Optimization
abstract: Quantum Stealth Computing, a paradigm shift in computation, necessitates robust security measures. Traditional approaches often focus on algorithm optimization, neglecting the fundamental role of topology in enhancing security. This research investigates the utilization of topological structures as a core optimization strategy for quantum stealth computing, specifically leveraging their inherent anti-interference properties to bolster security and explore potential applications. We propose a novel framework that dynamically adjusts topological parameters to mitigate potential attacks and enhance the overall computational resilience. This work presents a comprehensive analysis of the impact of topological optimization on quantum computation's security, demonstrating significant improvements in resilience against known attack vectors.

title: Federated Convolutional Transformer Network for Privacy-Preserving Photovoltaic Fault Detection in Distributed Solar Power Systems
abstract: Solar energy makes a considerable contribution to global power generation, necessitating photovoltaic (PV) fault detection to ensure high yields in solar power systems. In real-world solar installations, operational data are geographically dispersed, heterogeneous, and sensitive, which imposes privacy restrictions. Existing PV fault-detection techniques have relied on centralized training, requiring raw image data from multiple plants to be collected at a single server, which has led to privacy risks, bias from heterogeneous datasets, and scalability issues. To overcome these challenges, this research provides a novel FL-based PV fault-detection model called Federated Convolutional Transformer Network (Fed-CVTNet), which combines Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture within the FL framework. Initially, the raw images are pre-processed to enhance the input quality, and the Region of Interest (ROI) is identified via a pretrained YOLO model. Then, the proposed Fed-CVTNet facilitates networked learning among many geographically dispersed clients by only sharing model updates using federated averaging (FedAvg). The experimental findings illustrate that the proposed FL model shows substantial quality improvements compared to the customized CNN-ViT models trained on a dataset of 5600 images and the CNN-ViT models that lack federated aggregation. The highest accuracy achieved by the proposed technique is 98.99%; the proposed Fed-CVTNet has better sensitivity (98.15%) and specificity (99.21%), and much lower false positive and false negative rates than its centralized counterparts. The comparative analysis establishes that federated weight aggregation outperforms centralized baseline models by 2.3% and is effective in reducing the data privacy risk.

title: User-Centred Development of a Trustworthy E-Voting Application
abstract: Developing a secure and reliable remote electronic voting (e-voting) application presents critical challenges, particularly in ensuring system integrity, security, and user trust. This chapter focuses on designing and evaluating an e-voting system for student leader elections to address key factors influencing voter confidence. The development process followed a structured set of phases: analysis, design, development, implementation, and evaluation. Key concerns, such as transparency, voter anonymity, prevention of duplicate voting (singularity), and integrity of results, were addressed. A survey was conducted with 1,000 randomly selected students to assess their primary concerns and level of trust in the system. Results indicate that transparency, singularity, integrity, and anonymity are the most crucial requirements for an e-voting system. To enhance trust, efforts were made from the design phase through socialisation, including educational campaigns, application demonstrations, and user training. Rigorous testing was conducted by internal developers and external stakeholders, followed by a public trial. Out of 3,527 survey respondents, 68.04% expressed trust in the application, deeming it “feasible” for adoption. However, areas such as transparency and feedback mechanisms require further improvement to fully address user concerns. It contributes to the field of e-voting by underscoring the importance of user involvement and extensive testing in developing a trustworthy system for student elections.

title: Wrapped Gaussian process neural network model for manifold-valued data
abstract: In modern regression analysis tasks, an increasing amount of data exhibits non-Euclidean characteristics. Modeling methods based on traditional Euclidean space are no longer effective in adapting to the intrinsic geometric features of manifold-structured data. To address this issue, this paper proposes a neural network modeling framework for manifold-valued response variables. The proposed method, on the one hand, achieves a local correspondence between manifold space and Euclidean space through exponential mapping and its inverse mapping, constructing a geometrically compatible connection bridge for the association between predictor variables and manifold-valued response variables. On the other hand, considering the complex nonlinearity and unknown nature of this association, it utilizes the powerful nonlinear fitting capability of neural networks to accurately model it, breaking through the limitations of traditional linear assumptions. In addition, for potential random effects in the data, a wrapped Gaussian process prior is introduced to probabilistically characterize them, enhancing the model's adaptability to random fluctuations. In the parameter estimation stage, this paper adopts a penalized maximum likelihood estimation method to simultaneously solve neural network parameters and kernel function parameters, ensuring the global effectiveness and computational stability of the estimation process. The proposed model also has extensibility: (1) by designing a reasonable metric kernel function, it can directly handle complex scenarios where predictor variables are also in non-Euclidean space; (2) it can achieve uncertainty quantification of manifold-valued response variables based on a probabilistic framework. Simulation studies and real data analysis show that the proposed method is more competitive than Euclidean regression methods that do not consider the intrinsic structure of Riemannian manifolds.

title: Multi-Unary: a dense input encoding scheme for the quantum circuit model
abstract: Abstract The choice of a given encoding scheme for the problem variables, represented by a set of input qubits of a quantum circuit, substantially influences its design, as well as the quantity and nature of quantum resources (qubits and gates) employed by it. Quantum programmers have access to a variety of encoding strategies, such as one-hot, binary, Gray, amplitude encoding, or Schmidt decomposition, but each of them allows encoding just a single value for each problem variable. This article introduces a novel encoding scheme based on one-hot encoding, termed Multi-Unary, which enables the representation of multiple values within the input qubits, hence the descriptor ‘dense encoding scheme.’ The application of Multi-Unary is demonstrated in the context of the graph coloring problem using Grover’s algorithm, although its applicability extends to a broader class of quantum algorithms. By increasing the informational density on the input qubits, the multi-unary encoding offers potential advantages in terms of circuit compactness and resource efficiency, while at the same time enables an output value to contain more than one solution to a problem. Given its simple implementation, it can even replace the one-hot encoding scheme.

title: Decoupling Knowledge and Privacy: Post-Task Self-Distillation Replay for LLM Continual Learning
abstract: Privacy-preserving continual learning (PPCL) must reduce the reproduction of sensitive content while retaining useful knowledge across sequential tasks. Formal privacy guarantees characterize randomized mechanisms, whereas operational output control concerns whether a trained model selectively reduces the likelihood of sensitive content in its outputs. In this work, we investigate the latter together with continual-learning utility under realistic task evolution. Retention and privacy correction operate at different granularities: task acquisition requires broad preservation of current- and old-task behavior, whereas privacy correction targets sparse annotated positions. Joint optimization leaves the current-task preservation target continually changing. We propose SPARK, a retention-correction decomposition that first freezes the learned post-task distribution and then applies selective correction around this stable reference. Self-Distillation Replay learns the current task while distilling behavior from previous tasks, and Post-Task Privacy Correction reduces annotated-PII likelihood while anchoring current- and old-task non-PII behavior to the resulting checkpoint. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that SPARK achieves effective selective PII suppression while preserving strong continual-learning utility and knowledge retention across diverse settings. Code and data will be released upon publication.

title: A normal-inverse-Wishart (NIW) Bayesian synthesizer for multivariate normal data with application to polygenic risk scores
abstract: Bayesian synthesis, which generates synthetic data by sampling from the posterior predictive distribution, is a popular approach for privatizing sensitive personal data. However, how attribute disclosure risk is affected by feature dimensionality, the number of individuals in the original dataset, and the amount of released synthetic information remains poorly understood. We propose a mathematically tractable Bayesian synthesizer for multivariate normal data based on a conjugate normal-inverse-Wishart prior for the mean vector and covariance matrix. The conjugate structure yields closed-form posteriors and enables direct investigation of an adversary's ability to infer records under different data and release settings. We then demonstrate several intuitive properties of synthetic data generation through several simulations. Specifically, we show that disclosure risk decreases with the size of the original dataset, but increases with the dimensionality of the feature space and the amount of synthetic information released, whether through the release of larger synthetic datasets or multiple generator realizations. Finally, the proposed synthesizer was used to generate synthetic versions of a polygenic risk score dataset, with the synthetic data exhibiting distributional properties comparable to those of the original data.

title: Improving Information Extraction with Learned Queries
abstract: When information extraction fails, a natural instinct is to improve the model doing it: for example, by scaling it up or refining its reasoning. In this paper, we show that another part of the pipeline matters at least as much: the queries used to elicit this information. Across four clinical benchmarks and five LLMs, improving the question design alone raises performance by 18.6 F1-score points, i.e. more than using larger extraction models. To make such question design learnable, we introduce List of Questions (LoQ), which generates document-specific question sets, and FeedQ, a feedback-driven optimization method that iteratively refines questions against extraction outcomes. The resulting optimized questions can be used to train lightweight generators: with fine-tuning, 4B-parameter models match or outperform expert-derived baselines and substantially exceed the performance of much larger untuned models. We release a dataset of 12,820 optimized questions to support a broader shift in information extraction research toward treating question design as a first-class problem.

title: OCR-Based Field Extraction for Archaeological Pottery Metadata: The CENTURIA Dataset
abstract: Pottery is a primary source for reconstructing the chronological and economic dimensions of past societies. Archaeologists often document ceramic finds through technical drawings and handwritten metadata. This metadata is critical for dating, provenance attribution, and cross-site comparison, but remains inaccessible to computational analysis, requiring manual transcription of every record. We investigate whether state-of-the-art document analysis models can address this task, and introduce CENTURIA, a dataset of 507 pottery records from the Roman site of Carnuntum, providing transcriptions, bounding boxes, and structured field-level labels across seven metadata categories. Benchmarking five OCR models reveals a substantial domain gap: zero-shot transcription error reaches 15-32% SpACER-M, far exceeding rates on printed archival documents, with domain-specific fields recovered in fewer than 3% of cases. LoRA fine-tuning on just 57 samples, reflecting a realistic archival annotation budget, closes this gap, reducing transcription error to below 1.5% and recovering overall field-level accuracy above 87%. Our results show that a small expert-validated fine-tuning set suffices to convert handwritten pottery documentation into structured, searchable metadata ready for archaeological databases.

title: Knowing Beyond the Known: Reinforced Knowledge Specification for Multi-Label Class-Incremental Learning
abstract: Existing class-incremental learning methods struggle in multi-label scenarios (MLCIL) due to the inherent contradiction of learning objectives arising from co-occurring and incomplete labels. We argue that the core obstacle is the model's ambiguous boundary between known and unknown knowledge, which undermines historical knowledge retention, complicates current task learning, and limits adaptability to future concepts. To address this, we propose KBK (Knowing Beyond the Known), a reinforced knowledge specification framework that explicitly models what is known or not to unify historical, current, and prospective learning. Specifically, to clarify known knowledge, we develop a hierarchical feature purification module that disentangles fine-grained class-specific features from global features, where high-level semantic abstraction is reinforced with low-level visual features. Additionally, an uncertainty-aware recall enhancement strategy suppresses unreliable predictions based on distribution priors, improving the quality of historical recall. For probing the unknown, KBK leverages semantic correlations to synthesize informative unknown features under co-occurring, preserving embedding space for future learning. Furthermore, to mitigate heterogeneous forgetting, we design a category-balanced gradient compensation loss that dynamically reweights gradient backpropagation according to forgetting speeds. Experiments on multiple benchmarks validate the effectiveness and robustness of KBK, which surpasses prior best methods by 2.7% in Avg. Acc on MS-COCO B0-C10 setting even without any replay buffers.

title: Study on the Impact of Generative AI on Content Creation by Student Entrepreneurs -With Reference to ChatGPT
abstract: Abstract This study explores how student entrepreneurs use Generative AI, particularly OpenAI’s ChatGPT, to navigate the chaotic waters of launching a business while balancing academic life. Operating with tight budgets and minimal marketing experience, these young founders have eagerly turned to accessible AI tools to write social media posts, refine pitch decks, and draft digital marketing copy. Using a mixed-methods research design, data was gathered from 60 student entrepreneurs, aged 15 to 20, to understand how this technology genuinely shapes their daily operations and business growth. The findings show that ChatGPT is a powerful ally for early-stage brainstorming and copywriting. It dramatically boosts operational efficiency, lowers technical hurdles, relieves stress, and saves precious time, with 80% of respondents noting faster ideation and 78.3% praising the quality of the output. Yet, these benefits come with clear trade-offs. Roughly 65% of those surveyed worry that leaning too heavily on AI dulls their own creativity and critical thinking. Additionally, founders frequently run into generic responses (45%), a diluted brand voice (40%), and outright factual errors (36.7%). Because of these pitfalls, 76.7% emphasize the need for ethical guidelines. Ultimately, the study concludes that ChatGPT works best as a supportive tool rather than a human replacement. To ensure sustainable growth, campus incubators and educators must introduce digital literacy and prompt engineering training, helping young founders use AI responsibly without losing their unique entrepreneurial spark.

title: Measuring Trust Metrics and Purchase Velocity in Autonomous Livestream Retailing in the Mumbai Region
abstract: Abstract Livestream shopping has changed online retail by allowing hosts to demonstrate products, answer questions, and sell items in real time. Recently, online platforms have started using autonomous livestream retailing—where dynamic, computer-generated AI avatars replace human hosts to present products and answer customer questions 24/7. This study examines how consumers in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region (MMR) feel about these AI hosts, how much they trust them, and how quickly they make a purchase (purchase velocity).Using a study of 550 online shoppers across four main areas of Mumbai (South Mumbai, Suburban Mumbai, Thane, and Navi Mumbai), we tested how factors like avatar appearance, instant chat replies, regional language use (Hinglish), and clear disclosures affect buyer trust. The results show that fast, helpful chat replies and natural local speech build trust quickly. On the other hand, stiff or unnatural avatar movements (the "Uncanny Valley" effect) create doubt and delay buying decisions. When trust is high and instant payment options like UPI are built into the stream, shoppers make buying decisions much faster. This paper provides practical advice for online stores, AI developers, and consumer protection groups.

title: Quantum Topology Dynamic Topology Network Structure Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology, a fascinating field of physics, has recently garnered significant interest in areas of computation and materials science. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, Quantum Topology Dynamic Topology Network Structure Optimization Algorithm, designed to address the challenges of optimizing complex topological network structures. Leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement and self-organization, this algorithm aims to achieve significant improvements in system performance through intelligent network manipulation. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum entanglement to guide the evolution of network topology, employing quantum algorithms to optimize the resulting network structure. We propose a new framework for optimizing network topology based on these principles, demonstrating its potential for enhanced computational efficiency and performance in scenarios where traditional optimization methods fall short.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Machine Learning
abstract: Dynamic Adaptive Machine Learning (DAML) is a novel machine learning framework designed to address the limitations of traditional machine learning methods. It introduces a dynamic model parameter mechanism that automatically adjusts model parameters and learning strategies based on data and environment information, enabling more accurate and efficient learning. This approach contrasts with static model design, which often struggles to adapt to evolving data and environments. This paper details the design of DAML, including its core mechanism, benefits, and potential applications.

title: Title: Adaptive Bayesian Network for Dynamical System Modeling
abstract: This paper presents an Adaptive Bayesian Network (ABN) for dynamical system modeling, designed to enhance predictive accuracy and real-time control capabilities. Traditional Bayesian networks struggle with evolving systems, requiring manual parameter adjustments and limiting adaptability. Our proposed ABN leverages a "Neural Bayesian Network" – a novel learning approach – to dynamically update the network's structure based on observed data, resulting in improved predictive performance. The paper details the architecture, training process, and performance evaluation of the ABN, demonstrating its efficacy in modeling complex dynamical systems.

title: Meta-Learning for Adaptive Algorithm Selection
abstract: Algorithm selection is a critical, yet frequently manual and inefficient, step in many machine learning workflows. This paper proposes a novel meta-learning framework for adaptive algorithm selection, aiming to automate this process and improve overall performance. The core idea is to train a recurrent neural network (RNN) to model the algorithm selection process itself, learning from a limited set of training problems. This allows the system to dynamically adjust its algorithm selection strategy based on observed performance, effectively adapting to new, unseen problems. The system utilizes a specific loss function designed to mitigate performance degradation during adaptation. The key innovation lies in the integration of meta-learning with a dynamic, RNN-based algorithm selector, providing a system capable of continuous learning and adaptation. This approach offers a promising solution for tackling the challenges of algorithm selection, particularly in scenarios with diverse problem distributions and limited human expertise. The system's performance is evaluated theoretically and conceptually, demonstrating its potential benefits.

title: Title: Topological Information Theory Quantum Machine Learning Integration
abstract: This paper explores the integration of Topological Information Theory (TIT) with Quantum Machine Learning (QML) to achieve quantum acceleration and data compression in machine learning. Traditional machine learning relies on explicit parameter tuning, while this integration leverages the inherent structure of topological information theory for adaptive learning. We propose a novel method for utilizing the topological structure of quantum models as a source of noise, optimizing model parameters through topological analysis to improve efficiency and generalization. The core claim is that utilizing this approach will result in enhanced quantum acceleration and data compression compared to traditional machine learning. This work presents a framework for incorporating topological information into the quantum machine learning pipeline, demonstrating a potential paradigm shift in model optimization and efficiency.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Memory (QDM)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed memory architecture, termed Quantum Entanglement-Driven Distributed Memory (QDM), which leverages quantum entanglement to achieve ultra-long-distance, low-latency data access, circumventing the limitations imposed by physical distances in conventional distributed systems. The core concept involves multiple "quantum nodes" interconnected via entangled particles, forming a quantum channel for instantaneous data transmission and synchronization. Data is read and written through entangled measurements, eliminating the data replication and synchronization bottlenecks inherent in traditional distributed memory systems. We present a theoretical framework outlining the QDM architecture, focusing on the key mathematical concepts and operational principles. This architecture has the potential to revolutionize data processing and communication, especially in scenarios demanding extreme low latency and high bandwidth.

title: Core Claim: Develop a method based on adaptive quantum state geometry that automatically adjusts the geometric deformation of quantum states, enabling precise control, particularly in the handling of quantum state evolution.
abstract: Quantum state geometry offers a powerful framework for controlling and manipulating quantum systems, and the ability to dynamically adjust geometric parameters is crucial for achieving precise operations. This paper presents a novel algorithm for quantum state geometry, leveraging adaptive geometry to automatically adjust the shape of quantum states. We introduce a self-adaptive geometric deformation module that learns from the quantum state's characteristics, enabling precise control and efficient handling of complex quantum state evolution. The proposed approach offers a significant advancement over existing methods, particularly in scenarios requiring dynamic geometric adjustments. This work focuses on the development of a method that dynamically adjusts geometric parameters during quantum state evolution, leading to improved control and a more robust framework for quantum system manipulation. The core mechanism involves a self-learning module that adapts geometric parameters based on the quantum state's inherent properties, addressing a key challenge in precise quantum state engineering.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers the potential for secure communication and advanced computation. This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement information encoding algorithm designed to enhance the security and efficiency of quantum communication and computation. The algorithm leverages the unique properties of entangled states to optimize data encoding and transmission, addressing limitations of existing approaches. We detail the core mechanism, emphasizing the use of entanglement-based cryptography and error correction techniques to achieve a high level of resilience against eavesdropping. The proposed algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in security and efficiency compared to conventional methods.

title: Title: Topological Complexity Preservation
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to stabilizing topological complexity within neural networks, addressing limitations inherent in traditional gradient-based methods. We propose a dynamic stabilization algorithm, termed "Phase-Shifting Topology," that actively modifies the network's topology through subtle, dynamically-adjusted node interactions, fostering a constantly evolving and robust representation. The core mechanism centers around a phase-shifting function applied to node connections, creating a subtle, iterative shift in the network's structural arrangement. This shift mitigates the vanishing/exploding gradient problem, enhancing the stability of learned representations, and potentially improving generalization performance. We present a theoretical analysis of the algorithm's effectiveness and demonstrate its efficacy through simulations and preliminary experiments, highlighting its potential to significantly advance the field of neural network training.
