title: ## The Orangutan-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (OASA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Orangutan-Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (OASA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging and social dynamics observed in Sumatran orangutans. OASA leverages the observed strategies of orangutans, including resource prioritization, hierarchical decision-making, and adaptable movement patterns, to construct a robust and efficient search process. The algorithm incorporates three key mechanisms: a resource-aware prioritization scheme, a layered decision-making structure mimicking orangutan social hierarchies, and a dynamic adaptation of exploration and exploitation based on environmental feedback, similar to how orangutans adjust their behavior to changing food availability. The core of OASA lies in its adaptive parameter control, which adjusts exploration and exploitation rates based on the perceived "richness" of the search space, mirroring an orangutan's ability to identify and focus on promising areas. This paper outlines the algorithm's theoretical framework, detailing its components and operational principles. It aims to provide a foundational understanding of OASA and its potential applications in various optimization problems.

title: EvLink: Source-Grounded Evidence Linking for Graph RAG
abstract: Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) supports multi-hop reasoning by organizing corpora into structured graphs. However, graph reachability often captures semantic association rather than evidence support, so a reachable passage may still fail to justify a required cross-passage transition. We propose EvLink, an evidence-linking retriever that preserves passages as retrievable evidence units and builds evidence-supported transitions between them. EvLink constructs two types of reliable links: relation-grounded evidence links justified by explicit source relations, and endpoint-alignment links serving as sourcebounded fallbacks. For retrieval, we introduce a two-stage retrieval strategy. First, bounded breadth-first search over source-grounded evidence links recovers bridge passages missed by similarity-based methods. Then, evidenceneed mining with noisy-OR coverage refinement selects a compact, non-redundant evidence set satisfying distinct question facets. Experiments on three multi-hop and two simple QA benchmarks show EvLink consistently outperforms leading GraphRAG baselines with average gains of 2.4 R@5, 1.9 EM, and 2.4 F1

title: Universal Transformers for Circuit Computations: Perfect Length Generalization in Tiny Transformers
abstract: Learning generalizable algorithmic computations remains a challenge for neural networks, as reflected in persistent failures on compositional and length generalization benchmarks. We present a provably correct, transformer parameterization (with only 280 learnable parameters for Boolean algebra tasks) capable of learning and evaluating problems of any depth or length. We assume inputs are fully parenthesized, well-formed expressions. Our approach conceptualizes algorithmic tasks as circuit models embedded in transformers, enabling depth-1 circuit reduction in a single forward pass. To achieve depth generalization, we introduce a positional encoding that tracks each gate's depth within the circuit, enabling the model to identify evaluable subexpressions at each iteration via masked hard attention, with $O(n)$ per-iteration complexity via linear attention. Combined with an autonomous halting criterion, the model terminates after $d$ iterations for problems of depth $d$, yielding $O(n \cdot d)$ total complexity. We show that training on shallow problem instances (depth 1 and depth 2) effectively recovers interpretable parameters that {\em snap} into place, resulting in exact length generalization. Though we establish that our construction provably evaluates Boolean expressions -- a universal symbolic computation -- of arbitrary length perfectly, in other experiments we also demonstrate that our transformer variant can learn and generalize perfectly (100% accuracy) on other common length generalization benchmarks, including modular arithmetic and ListOps.

title: What Emerges and What Breaks in Self-Play Driving
abstract: Training autonomous driving policies through pure self-play has recently shown promising results. Following Gigaflow and Puffer- Drive, we train driving policies in a similar self-play fashion, but extend the models from MLPs to Transformers and train on the high-definition map of a real city, where we ultimately aim to deploy them. On the CARLA and Waymax benchmarks, our policies fall short of Gigaflow, and we trace the gap to specific failure modes, including reward hacking at traffic lights and a missing incentive to stop at stop signs. We further analyze which traffic rules emerge from self-play and how closely they match human driving, and we confirm that reward conditioning yields the intended diversity of driving behaviors. A demonstration of a trained policy is available at https://laursisask-ut.github.io/eccvdemo.

title: Modality Disentangled Learning for Incomplete Multimodal Emotion Recognition: A Primitive Memory Distillation Perspective
abstract: Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) systems often suffer from missing modalities in real-world scenarios. Existing methods usually generate, align, or distill missing modalities as a whole, overlooking the heterogeneous nature of the information carried by each modality. Such holistic treatment mixes inferable shared semantics with uncertain modality-specific details, yielding unstable representations and degrading robustness. To address this issue, we propose the Primitive Memory Distillation (PriMD) framework. Unlike existing methods, PriMD takes an intra-modal perspective and focuses on how different types of information within a modality differ in recoverability within each modality. PriMD first disentangles cross-modal shared semantics from modality-specific representations, and then discretizes the latter into learnable semantic primitives to construct modality-specific memory banks. When modalities are missing, PriMD is a teacher-student framework that the student model uses the shared semantics of available modalities as queries to dynamically retrieve primitives. It compensates for missing modality-specific information within a constrained memory space and aligns with the teacher model. Extensive experiments on IEMOCAP, CMU-MOSI, and CMU-MOSEI demonstrate that PriMD achieves state-of-the-art performance and consistently stronger robustness across a wide range of missing-modality settings, while mitigating the instability caused by holistic feature inference. Our code and project website are available at https://github.com/JiaqiZhang-Sengoku/PriMD and https://jiaqizhang-sengoku.github.io/PriMD/, respectively.

title: Quantum Imaginary Time Evolution on an Infinite 1D Chain
abstract: We introduce a quantum-circuit algorithm for performing imaginary-time evolution on infinite one-dimensional lattice systems. The method uses a parameterized quantum circuit to represent a uniform matrix product state ansatz. We derive the ITE algorithm using the time-dependent variational principle and employ the quantum Lanczos algorithm to improve the ground-state energy estimate. As a benchmark, we simulate the transverse-field Ising model using both classical simulators and IBM Quantum devices. Our analysis includes a statistical study of the distributions of the cost function and energy density obtained from quantum measurements, illustrating the effects of finite-sampling noise on convergence.

title: Rethinking PEFT Evaluation: A Class-Balanced Protocol Across Data Scales for Fair Comparison
abstract: 본 논문은 데이터 양(10%~100%)과 클래스 균형 여부를 독립적으로 통제하는 데이터 규모 별 클래스 균형 평가 프로토콜을 VTAB-1k 벤치마크에서 제안한다. 최근 대규모 사전학습 모델을 적은 비용으로 특정 데이터셋에 적응시키는 파라미터 효율적 미세조정(PEFT)이 주목받고 있으나, 의료·위성 영상과 같이 데이터가 극히 제한되고 클래스가 불균형한 현실적 환경에서의 학습 및 예측양상은 충분히 규명되지 않았다. 제안하는 프로토콜은 동결된 ViT 백본 위에서 주요 PEFT 기법(Adapter, LoRA, VPT)을 자연·특수·구조적 도메인의 19개 데이터셋에 대해 동일 조건에서 벤치마크하고, 완전 미세조정 및 linear probing baseline과 최신 변형 기법 DoRA를 함께 비교한다. 실험 결과, 데이터가 50%보다 적을 때는 특수·구조적 도메인에 강한 VPT가, 그보다 많을 때는 자연 도메인에 강한 LoRA가 우세하여 데이터 양에 따라 유리한 기법이 달라졌다. 또한 클래스 수를 맞춘 균형 학습은 데이터가 적을 때 전체 Top-1 정확도를 조금 낮추는 대신 모든 클래스를 고르게 평가하는 balanced accuracy를 높였고, 데이터가 많아지면 균형 데이터가 원본과 거의 같아져 그 효과가 사라졌다. 이처럼 모든 상황에서 가장 좋은 단일 PEFT 기법은 존재하지 않으며, 본 연구를 통해 도메인 특성·데이터 규모·클래스 분포에 따른 실용적 기법 선택 지침을 제시하여 의료·원격탐사·산업 검사 등 데이터가 제한된 다양한 응용 분야에서 PEFT의 효율적 적용에 기여할 수 있다.

title: E-Diagnose System Untuk Mendiagnosis Hama Dan Penyakit Pada Jenis Buah Alpukat Mentega Menggunakan Metode Dempster Shafer
abstract: Buah Alpukat mentega merupakan salah satu jenis buah alpukat yang berasal dari benua Amerika yang banyak dibudidaya di Indonesia. Namun, masalah yang terjadi adalah banyaknya pembudidaya ataupun petani tanaman alpukat mentega yang masih awam terhadap hama dan penyakit yang menyerang tanaman alpukat mentega. Minimnya pengetahuan dan belum memiliki pengalaman menjadi salah satu faktor penghambat para pembudidaya tanaman alpukat mentega untuk mendapatkan hasil panen yang terbaik. Biasanya, tanaman yang akan terjangkit sebuah hama dan penyakit akan menunjukkan gejala-gejala tertentu, akan tetapi banyak petani yang belum sadar atau membiarkan gejala tersebut. Oleh karena itu maka dibutuhkan sebuah Sistem Pakar berbasis web yang dapat digunakan oleh masyarakat umum khususnya para petani alpukat mentega untuk melakukan diagnosa terhadap hama dan penyakit tanaman alpukat mentega. Sistem pakar akan memberi daftar gejala-gejala sampai dapat mengidentifikasikan suatu kemungkinan diagnosa akan sebuah hama dan penyakit yang dikombinasikan dengan Metode Dempster Shafer. Hasil dari penelitian ini yaitu berdasarkan data sampel gejala yang dihitung yang terdiri dari: G01, G03, G04, G06 dan G13, hasil diagnosis pada sistem sama dengan hasil diagnosis yang dilakukan secara manual menggunakan Metode Dempster Shafer. Tanaman terdiagnosis penyakit P02 yaitu Hama Kutu Putih (Pseudococcus Spp.) dengan persentase 54%.

title: Sentiment To Strategy: A Business Intelligence Framework for Analyzing Consumer Trust in India's E-Commerce Sector Using Public Review Data
abstract: Abstract India's aspiration for Viksit Bharat @2047 designates e-commerce and the broader digital economy as important drivers of inclusive development, with consumer confidence acknowledged as the primary limitation on the sector's ongoing growth, especially in Tier-2 and Tier-3 areas. This study formulates and implements a Business Intelligence (BI) methodology to measure consumer trust extensively through publicly accessible e-commerce review data. The research utilizes a dataset comprising 361,219 refined Flipkart product reviews across 1,175 products, employing VADER (Valence Aware Dictionary and sEntiment Reasoner) sentiment analysis on the review text and juxtaposing the derived sentiment classification with customer-assigned star ratings to pinpoint instances of divergence between the two signals. The examination additionally develops keyword-driven trust-indicator flags (addressing counterfeit issues, product impairment, shipping delays, and return/refund complications) and consolidates results at both the product and price-band tiers. Research indicates that 77.3% of evaluations are deemed positive in sentiment; however, a significant 3.08% of all reviews demonstrate a discrepancy between star ratings and sentiment, suggesting that star ratings alone fail to fully capture consumer trust. Analysis at both the product and price-band levels indicates that trust signals differ significantly throughout categories and price tiers, with some products exhibiting elevated negative sentiment rates despite having commendable average star ratings. The document culminates by suggesting this BI framework as an effective, economical monitoring instrument that platforms, vendors, and policymakers, including entities linked to the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC) and the Digital India Mission, might implement to enhance consumer confidence and foster the sustainable development of India's e-commerce industry under Viksit Bharat @2047.

title: Revisión del estado actual de la Inteligencia Artificial en Bolivia
abstract: This study presents a review of the current state of artificial intelligence in Bolivia between 2024 and 2026, covering adoption, research and development, computing infrastructure, human resource development, governmental and business applications, governance, and regional positioning. The review draws on government sources, multilateral organizations, regional indicators, scientific publications, technical repositories, university initiatives, and records of digital infrastructure. The evidence is analyzed according to different levels of technological capability, distinguishing between the consumption of AI tools, the integration of existing models, machine learning applications, fine-tuning, and the development of foundation models. The results indicate an ecosystem that is still classified as exploratory within the Latin American context, characterized by growing adoption of generative AI and institutional applications, but limited capacity in research, specialized training, data governance, and accelerated computing infrastructure. Local initiatives were identified in computer vision, natural language processing, applied machine learning, remote sensing, and economic analysis, alongside professional data centers and an emerging regulatory agenda. However, no public evidence was found of the training of Bolivian foundation models or of GPU clusters operating at a scale comparable to the leading AI hubs in Latin America. The review indicates that Bolivia is transitioning from a stage of fragmented adoption toward the early construction of an institutional AI ecosystem, while remaining strongly dependent on technologies, models, and infrastructure developed abroad.

title: Arabic Emotion Classification Dataset for Large Language Model Evaluation
abstract: This dataset contains 1,002 Arabic text samples annotated for five emotion categories: anger, neutral, joy, sadness, and fear. The dataset was collected and initially annotated by Shaima Alzubi, with a second independent annotation performed by Mohammed Almehrzi. Annotation disagreements were reviewed and adjudicated by Fady Alnajjar. The annotation process was conducted under the supervision of Fady Alnajjar, Omar Mubin, and Ons Al-Shamaileh. The dataset was prepared to support the evaluation of large language models and Arabic language models for emotion classification. It accompanies the study “Deployment-Oriented Evaluation of Large Language Models for Arabic Emotion Classification.” The dataset includes the Arabic text samples and their corresponding gold-standard emotion labels. It is intended for research on Arabic natural language processing, emotion recognition, text classification, and benchmarking of large language models.

title: Quantum Information Cryptography: A Probabilistic Adaptive Key Generation Approach
abstract: Quantum information cryptography represents a paradigm shift in secure communication, leveraging the unique properties of quantum mechanics to create unbreakable encryption. This paper introduces a novel quantum information cryptographic system based on probabilistic adaptive key generation, aiming to enhance security and adaptability through the utilization of quantum entanglement. We propose a mechanism that dynamically adjusts key parameters based on observed security threats, ensuring resilience against evolving attacks. The system utilizes quantum state manipulation to generate keys, offering a significant advancement over traditional methods. This approach addresses the limitations of static key generation and provides a framework for robust and adaptable cryptographic solutions. The core concept hinges on the inherent vulnerability of existing classical key generation techniques when subjected to sophisticated attacks. This research explores the practical implications of this dynamic key generation system, detailing its architecture, operational mechanism, and preliminary security analysis.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Probability Model
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a bizarre phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate, has captivated physicists and philosophers alike. This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum entanglement to revolutionize probability theory and, consequently, quantum computation. We propose a novel probabilistic model predicated on the inherent nature of quantum entanglement, aiming to provide a deeper understanding of probability and enhance quantum machine learning capabilities. The core of this work lies in establishing a probabilistic model intrinsically linked to the quantum entanglement mechanism, offering a fundamentally new approach to interpreting and optimizing quantum computations. The model will be designed to function as a computational foundation for quantum algorithms, addressing the limitations of traditional probabilistic methods. This paper will detail the theoretical framework, preliminary implementation, and potential applications of this new model.

title: Dimension Generalization and Quantum Geometry Integration
abstract: The traditional approach to dimension generalization, often relying on simplified mathematical models, struggles to accurately predict computational outcomes. Quantum geometry's inherent self-adaptation offers a novel framework for tackling this challenge, enabling the creation of computations exceeding the limits of classical physics. This paper explores the integration of dynamic dimension generalization, driven by quantum entanglement, to achieve computational capabilities beyond current limitations. We introduce a novel algorithm that leverages this self-adaptation, aiming to push the boundaries of what's computationally feasible. The research is driven by the desire to explore a fundamental shift in how we approach complex calculations, potentially unlocking new frontiers in scientific and technological advancement.

title: Adaptive Non-Linear Transformation Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive optimization method for non-linear transformations, leveraging dynamic adjustment of the optimization objective based on the relationship between input data and the transformation itself. Traditional optimization techniques often require manual rule design, limiting efficiency. Our approach automatically adjusts the optimization rules to achieve superior performance. The core mechanism involves a dynamically adjusted transformation function, resulting in more efficient transformations. This work addresses the limitations of existing methods by providing a flexible and automated optimization strategy, potentially applicable to diverse transformation tasks. The proposed method demonstrates improved results compared to established techniques, particularly in scenarios with complex input data.

title: Title: Dynamic Topology Generation for Adaptive Algorithms
abstract: Dynamic Topology Generation for Adaptive Algorithms addresses the challenge of ensuring adaptability in complex algorithms by creating and adjusting a topology dynamically based on input data. This paper introduces a novel algorithm that learns to generate and refine the topology of an adaptive algorithm, improving its performance and resilience across diverse datasets. We present a methodology leveraging reinforcement learning to optimize the topology, fostering a more robust and adaptable system. This approach moves beyond static topology design, offering a truly dynamic and intelligent adaptation mechanism, crucial for navigating the complexities of real-world applications. The core mechanism focuses on iteratively refining the topology through feedback, resulting in improved performance and the ability to handle variations in input data. This work explores the potential of automated topology creation, paving the way for more efficient and adaptable algorithms.

title: Cognitive Architectures for AI Creativity – Bayesian Latent Variable Models
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of Bayesian Latent Variable Models (BLVMs) as a foundational approach for fostering artificial creativity. The central argument posits that AI creativity can be effectively nurtured by constructing cognitive architectures explicitly rooted in BLVMs. These architectures facilitate the exploration of novel ideas by leveraging probabilistic reasoning and the inherent uncertainty within complex systems. The proposed architecture integrates sensory input, internal representations, and a probabilistic inference engine, allowing the system to generate creative outputs. This approach represents a novel attempt to formalize and implement the creative processes observed in the human brain, providing a framework for AI systems to move beyond simple pattern recognition and towards genuine creative generation. The core contribution lies in the systematic design and implementation of a BLVM-based cognitive architecture specifically tailored for creative tasks, offering a theoretical and computational basis for understanding and replicating creative behavior in AI.

title: Title: Bayesian Geometric Chaos with Adaptive Constraint Propagation
abstract: Bayesian Geometric Chaos with Adaptive Constraint Propagation represents a novel approach to modeling complex systems, particularly those exhibiting intricate dynamics and high-dimensional parameter spaces. This paper explores the integration of a variational Bayesian framework, incorporating adaptive constraint propagation, to dynamically adjust model parameters and enhance prediction accuracy. Traditional Bayesian methods often fall short in these scenarios, struggling to effectively handle non-linearity and uncertainty. Our work proposes a fundamentally adaptive self-optimizing method, moving beyond static inference to a process where the model parameters are continually refined through a learned "chaos" function, guided by observed data. This leads to improved prediction capabilities across a range of applications, including fluid dynamics and protein folding simulations. The core mechanism leverages a variational Bayesian approach, utilizing observed data to update the model's parameters, and adaptive constraint propagation, which adjusts constraint parameters to guide the learning process. We demonstrate the efficacy of this framework through a series of simulations and analysis, highlighting its potential for addressing limitations of existing Bayesian methods.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Hierarchical Compositional Representations
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning by leveraging hierarchical compositional representations. The core idea is to integrate the pattern recognition capabilities of deep neural networks with the logical inference capabilities of symbolic reasoning engines. We introduce a system where a deep neural network learns hierarchical representations of knowledge, capturing statistical regularities from data. These representations are then utilized by a symbolic reasoning engine to perform logical deduction. The key innovation lies in the hierarchical structure, enabling the system to handle complex reasoning tasks and provide more explainable results. We formulate the system using the following key components and equations: Let *S* = {*s*1, *s*2, ..., *s*K} be the set of concepts. Let *R* = {*r*1, *r*2, ..., *r*N} be the set of relations. Let *H* be the hierarchical representation of knowledge. The system learns *H* from data *D* using a deep neural network *N*. The symbolic reasoning engine *E* performs logical deduction based on *H*. The system can be represented as: *E*( *H* ) = *Result*, where *Result* is the logical conclusion. The neural network *N* aims to minimize the error between its prediction and the ground truth, expressed as: || *N*( *D* ) - *Target* ||, where *Target* represents the desired output. The hierarchical representation *H* is constructed as: *H* = (*h*1, *h*2, ..., *h*M), where *h*i represents a node in the hierarchy. The logical deduction process can be formalized as: *Result* = *Deduce*( *H* ) using logical rules. The system's performance is evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. This approach offers a pathway towards more robust and explainable AI systems. ---

title: ## Black Lemur: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Black Lemur Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Black Lemur, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm's design is inspired by the foraging behavior of black lemurs, specifically their unique ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources in challenging environments. Black Lemur combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) with a novel memory mechanism mimicking the lemur's cognitive mapping of food locations. The core innovation lies in the algorithm's adaptive memory system, which dynamically adjusts its exploration and exploitation strategies based on the perceived landscape and the lemur's past foraging experiences. The performance of Black Lemur is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The key contributions of this work include a detailed algorithm description, a theoretical analysis of its convergence properties, and empirical validation through extensive testing. The algorithm's performance is compared with established metaheuristic methods, showcasing its potential for improved solution quality and efficiency.

title: Black Flying Fox Algorithm (BFA)
abstract: This paper presents the Black Flying Fox Algorithm (BFA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Black Flying Fox (Pteropus melanopterus). BFA leverages the bat's echolocation and flight patterns to explore the search space and converge towards optimal solutions. The algorithm incorporates key characteristics of bat behavior, including pulse rate modulation, frequency changes, and position adjustments, into a dynamic optimization framework. BFA utilizes a population-based approach, employing a swarm of candidate solutions represented as vectors. The algorithm's core mechanism involves iteratively updating the position and velocity of each bat based on its fitness and the global best solution. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BFA through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The algorithm's simplicity and adaptability make it a promising tool for a wide range of optimization challenges. The core mathematical formulation of BFA is presented, along with detailed explanations of the algorithm's parameters and their influence on performance. The analysis reveals that BFA's performance is strongly influenced by the pulse rate, frequency modulation parameters, and the diversity of the population.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Encoding: A Matrix Evolution Algorithm
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement to encode and process mathematical matrices, leveraging the instantaneous correlations inherent in this phenomenon. We explore a novel algorithm that employs a matrix evolution process guided by quantum entanglement, aiming to achieve unprecedented accuracy and computational speed in matrix calculations. The core mechanism centers around introducing quantum effects within a matrix evolution algorithm, driven by the entangled state of the matrix itself. This research delves into the theoretical and practical implications of this approach, with a particular focus on its potential for revolutionizing quantum computation. The study aims to demonstrate the feasibility of harnessing entanglement for significant advancements in matrix manipulation and information processing. The findings will address the challenges and opportunities presented by this paradigm shift in computational methods.

title: 基于自适应神经网络的概率推理算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic reasoning algorithm based on adaptive neural networks. Traditional probabilistic reasoning methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting their adaptability and hindering performance. Our approach leverages the concept of adaptive neural networks, dynamically adjusting network parameters to optimize inference accuracy and efficiency. The core mechanism involves a self-tuning parameter adjustment process, enabling the algorithm to adapt to the specific characteristics of the input data and improve reasoning capabilities. We present a comprehensive evaluation of our algorithm against established methods, demonstrating its superior performance in complex probabilistic scenarios. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications of this approach for various real-world applications.

title: Title: Adaptive Modeling Based on Dynamic Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic network model designed to enhance the precision of complex system modeling. Traditional network models often rely on static parameter settings, while this approach leverages a dynamic network model through parameter adjustment and structural change. The core mechanism involves employing a feedback loop that continuously refines the network's parameters and topology to achieve more accurate representations of intricate systems. We investigate the algorithm's effectiveness through a series of simulations, demonstrating improved performance compared to baseline models across a range of system types. The results highlight the potential of this dynamic approach to overcome limitations of static models, particularly in capturing the inherent variability within complex systems.

title: Betsileo Sportive Lemur: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Lemur Locomotion
abstract: This paper proposes a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Betsileo Sportive Lemur" (BSL), inspired by the unique locomotion strategies observed in lemurs, particularly those of the Betsileo lemur species. Lemurs exhibit remarkable agility, adaptability, and efficiency in their movements, which are crucial for survival in their complex environments. BSL leverages these observed behaviors to develop a novel optimization approach. The algorithm incorporates key aspects of lemur movement, including variable speed adjustments, directional shifts, and obstacle avoidance, into its core search mechanism. Specifically, BSL utilizes a dynamically adjusted velocity vector, inspired by the lemur's gait, and a probabilistic steering mechanism mimicking the lemur's ability to adjust its course based on environmental feedback. The performance of BSL is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's design prioritizes adaptability and robustness, aiming to improve convergence speed and solution quality. The core of BSL relies on a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating lemur-inspired heuristics. The results presented in this paper highlight the potential of bio-inspired algorithms in tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: 基于图的自适应数据压缩算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel data compression algorithm based on graph structure. Traditional data compression methods rely on manual parameter tuning, limiting their adaptability. This work introduces a self-adaptive compression technique that dynamically adjusts the compression ratio based on the inherent graph structure of the data. The algorithm leverages graph representation and node-based compression to achieve significantly improved compression efficiency and reduced storage costs. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through extensive experimental results on various data types, showcasing substantial gains in compression ratio and storage space compared to existing methods. The core mechanism centers around a graph representation and a compression ratio adjustment process driven by graph properties. This approach offers a more robust and adaptable solution for data compression, particularly for large and complex datasets.

title: Title: Quantum-Enhanced Generative Modeling via Variational Circuits
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum-enhanced generative modeling through the development of novel variational circuit-based models. We propose a new class of generative models that exploit quantum effects to improve sampling efficiency and feature extraction capabilities, moving beyond the limitations of classical generative techniques. The core mechanism centers on employing variational circuits to generate complex data, pushing the boundaries of what's currently achievable in generative modeling. The integration of quantum chemistry principles into variational circuit design allows for a pathway towards significantly enhanced data quality and representation. This work presents a theoretical framework and initial explorations demonstrating the potential of this approach, highlighting the advantages of quantum-enhanced generative modeling.

title: Nonlinear Geometry Topology and Quantum Entanglement Protocol Verification
abstract: This paper investigates the validation of a quantum entanglement protocol leveraging non-linear geometry and dynamic topology. We introduce a novel protocol that dynamically adjusts quantum state parameters to enhance entanglement fidelity. Furthermore, we develop a mechanism to quantitatively assess the quantum state's vulnerability to decoherence, driven by topological properties. The core claim is that this approach significantly improves entanglement quality and provides deeper insights into the quantum state's fragility. This work addresses a significant gap in current quantum information security and quantum computing strategies by moving beyond static qubit manipulation and embracing dynamic topology.

title: Dynamic Topology Quantum Network Routing
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to quantum network routing within a dynamic topology framework. The core concept revolves around leveraging the inherent properties of quantum topology, specifically exchange operations and entanglement, to construct a reconfigurable quantum network. The proposed routing algorithm dynamically optimizes the entanglement network path in real-time, aiming to achieve efficient quantum information transmission. The key innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of routes, a significant challenge currently addressed in topological quantum network research. This work presents a theoretical framework and a foundational routing algorithm, laying the groundwork for future research and development in resilient and adaptable quantum communication networks. The system utilizes a network represented as (S1, S2, ..., SK), where Si represents a node in the network. The routing algorithm is defined as φ(S1, S2, ..., SK), which returns a sequence of nodes representing the optimal path. The efficiency of the routing is measured by the average path length (L) and the number of exchanges (E) required. A key element is the concept of topological entanglement, denoted as Eij, representing the entanglement between nodes i and j. The routing algorithm aims to minimize the total path length while maximizing the utilization of topological entanglement. The core algorithm can be expressed as: φ(S1, S2, ..., SK) = argminP Σj=1N Lj(P), where P is a path from S1 to SK, and Lj(P) is the path length of path P. The minimization is performed subject to constraints related to topological entanglement and network topology.

title: Dynamic Quantum Topology Verification via Quantum Computation
abstract: Dynamic Quantum Topology Verification via Quantum Computation addresses the critical challenge of verifying complex quantum topology models, a bottleneck in quantum computing development. This paper proposes a novel approach that utilizes quantum computation to automate the generation of verification results, significantly enhancing the efficiency of the validation process. We present a framework that leverages the unique properties of quantum algorithms to efficiently test and validate the integrity of these models, ultimately contributing to a more robust and scalable quantum computing ecosystem. The core mechanism revolves around a quantum circuit-based verification protocol designed to identify inconsistencies and ensure the model's adherence to fundamental topological constraints. This research demonstrates the potential for automated verification, reducing the reliance on manual inspection and accelerating the development cycle.

title: Matrix Generation for Quantum Computing: A Novel Approach to Linear Equation Solving
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum computing approach leveraging the unique properties of matrix generators to efficiently solve specific types of linear equation problems, particularly those involving high-dimensional and complex matrices. The method employs quantum state generation and quantum algorithm implementation to provide a more efficient solution compared to traditional methods. We present a detailed explanation of the core mechanism, including the advantages of quantum state generation and the application of quantum algorithms to address linear equation problems. This research explores the potential of matrix generators as a foundation for accelerating linear equation solving within quantum computing.

title: 基于信息熵的程序优化算法
abstract: This paper proposes a novel program optimization algorithm based on information entropy. The core claim of this work is that information entropy can serve as a valuable metric for assessing program complexity and evaluating optimization effectiveness during the programming process. The algorithm leverages the concept of entropy to quantify the uncertainty or randomness associated with a program's state. By continuously monitoring and adjusting program parameters based on this entropy value, the system aims to converge towards an optimal solution. The methodology focuses on dynamically adapting the optimization process by considering the inherent complexity of the problem, offering a potentially more robust and efficient approach compared to traditional optimization techniques. This research introduces a new perspective on program optimization, utilizing a probabilistic measure – entropy – to guide the search for optimal program states. The presented algorithm's effectiveness will be demonstrated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, paving the way for future experimental validation.

title: ## Zebra Anemone Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ZIMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Zebra Anemone Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (ZIMA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Zebra Anemones. These anemones exhibit a sophisticated strategy for attracting and retaining symbiotic clownfish, utilizing color changes and subtle movements. ZIMA mimics this dynamic interaction by incorporating a concept of "attraction-repulsion" within a population of potential solutions. The algorithm employs a dynamic weight system to modulate the influence of attraction and repulsion, similar to how the anemone adjusts its behavior based on the presence and response of the clownfish. ZIMA aims to achieve efficient exploration and exploitation of the search space, leading to improved convergence rates and solution quality compared to traditional metaheuristic methods. This paper details the algorithm's design, core principles, and provides a theoretical framework for understanding its operation.

title: ## The Butterfly's Dance: An Evolutionary Algorithm Inspired by Eye Spots in *Papilio* Butterflies
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, termed "Butterfly's Dance" (BD), inspired by the visual communication strategy employed by *Papilio* butterflies – the use of eye spots to deter predators. BD leverages the concept of dynamic attraction and repulsion, mirroring the butterfly's movement pattern in response to perceived threats. The algorithm utilizes a population of candidate solutions, represented as vectors, and employs a novel attraction-repulsion mechanism based on the distance to a "threat" vector, dynamically adjusting the attraction and repulsion forces. The algorithm incorporates a mutation operator mimicking the erratic flight pattern of the butterfly, further enhancing its exploration capabilities. We present a theoretical framework for BD, detailing its core components and operational rules. While not yet validated through experimental testing, this paper lays the groundwork for future research and exploration of BD's potential in various optimization problems.

title: Andean Tapeti: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Andean Tapeti Weaving
abstract: This paper presents Andean Tapeti, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the intricate and adaptive process of Andean tapeti weaving. Tapeti weaving, a traditional craft practiced in the Andes, involves iteratively adding threads and patterns to a textile, responding to constraints and aiming for an aesthetically pleasing and functionally sound final product. Andean Tapeti leverages this process to develop a new optimization technique. The algorithm incorporates key features of tapeti weaving, including a thread selection mechanism based on a stochastic preference, a pattern insertion strategy that balances exploration and exploitation, and a dynamic adjustment of thread density based on a perceived level of convergence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Andean Tapeti through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization. The algorithm's adaptability and ability to handle complex constraints make it a promising candidate for a wide range of optimization applications.

title: # Amuyao Tree Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Mus sylvaticus*
abstract: This paper introduces Amuyao Tree Mouse (ATM), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Mus sylvaticus* (Tree Mouse). Tree Mice exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources within complex, tree-structured environments. ATM leverages this behavior by employing a tree-based representation of the search space and a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation strategy. The algorithm utilizes a novel "Root-Branch-Leaf" mechanism to guide the search process, mimicking the Tree Mouse's navigation and resource selection. Specifically, the algorithm maintains a tree structure representing potential solutions, dynamically adjusts the probability of exploring new branches versus exploiting existing ones based on a simulated "hunger" level, and incorporates a local search operator inspired by the Tree Mouse's sniffing behavior. We present a detailed description of the algorithm, its underlying principles, and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations on benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate that ATM performs competitively with established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization, while exhibiting potentially superior performance in certain problem landscapes. The key innovation lies in the tree structure and the dynamic adjustment of exploration-exploitation, offering a robust and adaptable approach to complex optimization challenges.

title: Quantum-Inspired Stochastic Gradient Descent for Deep Learning
abstract: Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) is a cornerstone algorithm in deep learning, widely employed for optimizing model parameters. However, SGD is susceptible to getting trapped in local minima, leading to suboptimal solutions and hindering the training process. This paper proposes a novel approach, Quantum-Inspired Stochastic Gradient Descent (QISGD), which leverages principles from quantum walks to enhance exploration and overcome the limitations of traditional SGD. The core idea is to adaptively adjust the learning rate based on the uncertainty associated with the gradient estimate, mirroring the probabilistic nature of quantum walks. Specifically, QISGD employs a stochastic update rule where the step size is dynamically modified, promoting wider exploration of the parameter space. The theoretical framework establishes connections between the proposed method and quantum walk concepts, highlighting its potential to improve training speed and convergence rates. We demonstrate, through analysis and mathematical formulation, that QISGD can effectively mitigate the issues of local minima and enhance the overall optimization performance of deep learning models. The presented formulation offers a new perspective on SGD, blending classical optimization with quantum-inspired concepts for enhanced training.

AVMA employs a combination of adaptive step-size control, a novel exploration-exploitation balance mechanism mimicking the vole's tendency to balance foraging with risk aversion, and a dynamic memory system that stores and utilizes information about past solutions. title: AI-Enabled Sustainable Digital Marketing Systems: A Stimulus–Organism–Response Framework of Customer Engagement and Institutional Sustainability Capabilities
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed digital marketing in so many ways because it enables intelligent, personalized, and data-driven customer experiences. Nonetheless, current research remains fragmented, mostly because it emphasizes the direct effect of AI on marketing performance while overlooking the instruments through which AI influences sustainable digital marketing systems (SDMSs) and the institutional conditions necessary for its proper usage. To fill in the gaps, this study develops and empirically tests an integrated Stimulus–Organism–Response (S–O–R) framework that conceptualizes AI-enabled sustainable digital marketing systems as the technological stimulus that influences sustainable digital marketing performance through customer satisfaction, customer engagement, and sustainable customer outcomes. The model incorporates sustainable customer outcomes and institutional sustainability capability as contextual constraints; it includes firm readiness and the regulatory environment as institutional sustainability capabilities that enable ethical and accountable AI integration. Using a quantitative, cross-sectional research design and survey data from 720 AI users, the model is analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The findings show that AI-enabled sustainable digital marketing systems can tremendously improve sustainable digital marketing performance both directly and indirectly through customer satisfaction, engagement, and loyalty. Strategic integration, institutional sustainability capabilities, and supportive regulatory environments further strengthen these relationships. The study strengthens the S–O–R framework by including technological, psychological, and institutional mechanisms into a unified model of sustainable digital marketing. It also accelerates responsible AI research by establishing how customer-centered AI deployment and institutional sustainability capabilities both promote long-term customer value creation and sustainable organizational performance. This provides practical guidance for developing ethical and sustainable AI-enabled marketing strategies.

title: Clustering and Principal Component Analysis as Distinct Computational Regimes of a Biologically Motivated Neural Circuit
abstract: Background: Characteristic circuitry in superficial layers of neocortex has been repeatedly shown to carry out lateral inhibition: excitatory–inhibitory interactions within a specific anatomical design. Methods: We provide simulation and formal analyses of the emergent operations of this circuitry. Results: Derived directly from anatomical circuit layout and physiological activation patterns, we show that this circuit carries out two distinct effective procedures on its inputs: categorization, and component analysis; moreover, we show that each procedure’s emergence is dependent on a single biological parameter: the relative strength of local feedback inhibitory cells. We characterize the detailed nature of both the biological activity and the emergent statistical operations and evaluate them in the context of extensive related literature in statistics, machine learning, and computational neuroscience. Conclusions: Very notably, the two emergent operations (clustering and component analysis) have not previously been shown to contain deep mathematical connections to each other, let alone to each be derivable from a single overarching algorithmic precursor that has clustering and component analysis as two special cases. The identification of that deep formal mathematical connection, and its arrival directly from a detailed biological circuit, represents a rare instance of novel mathematical relations arising from biological analyses.

title: Cognitive Decoupling and Compensatory Gains: An AI‐Enhanced Pedagogy for Bridging the Mathematical Gap in Signals and Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT The heavy mathematical requirements in Signals and Systems frequently prevent students from developing physical intuition. This study evaluates an Outcome‐Based Education framework implemented through a novel dual‐component architecture. This architecture pairs a RAG‐enabled Socratic Pedagogical Agent (SPA) with a dynamic visual platform to provide a safe‐failure environment for parameter exploration across four instructional stages: Perception, Exploration, Synthesis, and Transfer. A quasi‐experimental study with 192 students assessed this approach. The final evaluation isolated Procedural Fluency (55%), Analytical Derivation (25%), and Conceptual Mastery (20%). Despite entering with a statistically lower math baseline ( p < 0.001), the experimental group achieved statistical parity with the historical control in overall grades ( p = 0.724), Procedural Fluency ( p = 0.312), and Analytical Derivation ( p = 0.362). Crucially, the experimental cohort scored significantly higher in Conceptual Mastery ( p = 0.004, d = 0.42). The findings provide preliminary support for the compensatory hypothesis: pairing visual cognitive offloading with AI‐guided inquiry is associated with enhanced mastery of complex system dynamics for learners with weaker prior mathematical preparation, without degrading procedural skills. Finally, subjective evaluations revealed high student acceptance, with learners specifically valuing the safe‐failure environment over direct computational shortcuts.

title: Sequential knowledge editing breaks a model's ability to tell good evidence from bad, without costing it accuracy
abstract: Knowledge editing is evaluated on whether the edited fact changed, whether paraphrases follow, and whether unrelated answers stayed put. A model can pass all three and still lose something none of them measures: the ability to decide, on facts that were never edited, which retrieved documents to believe. We score the log odds a model assigns to its remembered answer against the answer an injected passage asserts, before and after editing, holding the query, the passage and both candidate strings fixed. Our cleanest arm is a conservatively tuned LoRA: after 1,000 sequential edits on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct it leaves MMLU unchanged to four decimal places, yet the spread of the arbitration quantity across untouched facts falls by 36%. Selective prediction degrades with it. Area under the risk-coverage curve rises by 0.107, against 0.005 for a norm-matched perturbation at the same MMLU, and error on the model's most confident quarter of arbitration decisions goes from 0.217 to 0.342. This is not capability loss. Sweeping random perturbation over five severities, damage bad enough to cut MMLU from 0.6275 to 0.3725 produces less harm (0.088) than MEMIT does at 0.6050 (0.102). The effect holds across three seeds, two model families, two datasets, two probe-disjointness criteria, three prompt templates and paraphrased queries. Layer ablation on saved weight deltas shows it is distributed: no single layer reproduces it, and removing any one recovers about half. Under retrieval with a frozen retriever, accuracy falls from 0.592 to 0.46. A secondary finding may matter more in practice. Three of five model and method pairings we ran collapse to chance MMLU at 1,000 sequential edits under published hyperparameters, while edit success stays at 1.00 and locality reads clean. Sequential-editing evaluations that never measure capability cannot see this.

title: AdaPath: Query-Adaptive Path-Finding via Path-Bank for Multi-Hop Implicit Biomedical KGQA
abstract: Path-finding over knowledge graphs has become an effective way to ground LLM reasoning on multi-hop questions. However, biomedical QA introduces two distinct challenges that general-domain methods are not designed for: (i) queries do not expose intermediate reasoning and can be answered through multiple valid pathways, and (ii) biomedical knowledge graphs are densely connected, so path-finding methods easily take wrong turns. To address these challenges, we propose AdaPath, a path-finding framework that retrieves query-adaptive meta-paths from Path-Bank, which captures both query semantics and biomedical knowledge graph structure. AdaPath provides the missing cues in biomedical queries while effectively pruning dense knowledge graph neighborhoods during multi-hop reasoning. We further release BioStrat-QA, a biomedical KGQA benchmark that stratifies multi-hop queries by how much intermediate reasoning they expose. Across biomedical KGQA benchmarks, AdaPath consistently outperforms baselines, sustaining meaningful path-finding even when multi-hop queries expose less surface information. The source code is available at https://github.com/Jun-Hyeong-Kim/AdaPath.

title: Analisis Sentimen Dan Pemodelan Topik Pada Ulasan Aplikasi WhatsApp Business
abstract: WhatsApp Business sebagai media pemasaran produk dan jasa, memiliki potensi besar dalam menjangkau konsumen karena dominasi penggunanya yang sangat masif di Indonesia. Untuk memahami seberapa baik pengimplementasian aplikasi tersebut dalam kegiatan bisnis, maka penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis persepsi pengguna aplikasi WhatsApp Business melalui pendekatan text mining, serta menggunakan model Indonesian RoBERTa Base untuk analisis sentimen dan BERTopic untuk pemodelan topik. Data penelitian sebanyak 10.000 ulasan pengguna WhatsApp Business diperoleh melalui teknik scraping pada platform Google Play Store. Data yang diperoleh kemudian diproses melalui tahapan pra-pemrosesan teks, dan selanjutnya dilakukan pelabelan otomatis berdasarkan tiga kategori sentimen (negatif, netral, dan positif). Hasil klasifikasi sentimen menunjukkan akurasi 94%, dengan nilai rata-rata F1-Score 0.94 yang menunjukkan konsistensi hasil prediksi pada ketiga kelas sentimen. Pemodelan topik pada sentimen negatif, diperoleh enam topik utama yang meliputi masalah media pengiriman file foto dan video, masalah spam, pemblokiran akun, pengiriman pesan, serta masalah katalog produk. Temuan ini diharapkan dapat menjadi bahan evaluasi bagi pengembang aplikasi (Meta/Facebook) untuk meningkatkan keandalan aplikasi WhatsApp Business. Kata Kunci: analisis sentimen, whatsapp business, indonesian roberta base, bertopic

title: Impacto en los procesos operativos y estratégicos de la experiencia del cliente (CX) mediante la implementación de la inteligencia artificial (IA): análisis bibliométrico y revisión sistemática de la literatura.
abstract: El propósito de esta investigación es analizar la implementación de la Inteligencia Artificial (IA) en la Experiencia del Cliente (CX). La introducción contextualiza la transición hacia la Experiencia Total (ET), destacando la tensión entre la eficiencia algorítmica y la necesidad de empatía humana, además del riesgo de reducir la libertad de elección del consumidor mediante filtros burbuja. La metodología adoptada es de carácter bibliométrico y sistemático, siguiendo el protocolo PRISMA 2020; se utilizaron herramientas como R-Studio y Biblioshiny para analizar 54 registros de Scopus y Academic (2021-2026), seleccionando un corpus final de 9 artículos de Scopus publicados en 2026 para un análisis profundo de co-ocurrencia y mapeo temático. Los resultados obtenidos en la revisión bibliométrica revelan un ecosistema de investigación emergente donde la IA y la CX son nodos centrales e indisolubles; se identificaron temas motor como el comportamiento del consumidor y temas emergentes como la privacidad de datos; se destaca la integración de los modelos TAM y SOR para equilibrar la eficiencia técnica con la respuesta emocional, subrayando la importancia del Reskilling y Upskilling de los empleados ante la automatización. Las conclusiones indican que la IA optimiza procesos operativos y estratégicos, pero su éxito depende de la coherencia en el ecosistema digital. Se propone evolucionar del trabajo en silos hacia una Experiencia Total que armonice la eficiencia técnica con la calidez humana, sugiriendo futuras investigaciones sobre el impacto emocional y patrones culturales en el uso de la IA

title: Grammatical Tagging of Arabic Word for Corpus Analysis
abstract: Word tagging is one of the important processes in computational linguistics studies. It provides detailed information about the grammatical part of speech (PoS) to the researcher. However, tagging process is not an easy process particularly when relating to Arabic text. One of the main reasons that led to this situation is the fact that many Arabic word characters (space between characters) could contain more than one word. Thus, this paper aims to revisit our experience in tagging Arabic words and to highlight critical issues related to the process. It also aims to validate the possibility of using computer analyzer software, namely Wordsmith 5.0 for Arabic texts. Using several Arabic texts from newspapers as examples, this paper reveals how the tagging process was executed using a self-constructed tag set. It also discusses the issues and linguistic factors considered in constructing the tag sets. This includes the differences that exist between Arabic word characteristics in writing and their articulation. This paper finally stresses the more complicated issues in tagging Arabic words in relation to the fact that Arabic has the affixation and diacritics systems. The application of short vowels and orthographic diacritics in Arabic language also contributes to the phenomenon. Despite this fact, this paper also proves that a researcher can make the tagging process simpler by focusing on certain grammatical features, aiming the tagging for word disambiguation and applying an appropriate analyzing software.

title: Role of AI In Viksit Bharat 2047
abstract: Abstract Artificial Intelligence (AI) is emerging as a transformative force in India’s journey towards achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. This paper examines the potential role of AI in accelerating economic growth, improving productivity, promoting innovation, strengthening public services, and supporting inclusive and sustainable development. It highlights the opportunities presented by AI across key sectors, including agriculture, healthcare, education, manufacturing, sustainability, smart cities, governance, and digital services. The study also discusses India’s growing position in the global AI landscape, supported by its skilled workforce, digital infrastructure, startup ecosystem, and government initiatives. The paper emphasizes that the successful adoption of AI requires more than technological advancement. Human-centred development, ethical governance, data security, digital inclusion, infrastructure development, workforce reskilling, and collaboration among government, industry, academia, and citizens are essential for ensuring that the benefits of AI reach diverse sections of society. Particular attention is given to challenges such as infrastructure gaps, talent retention, employment disruption, data sovereignty, regulatory requirements, and unequal access to AI technologies. The paper further proposes a strategic roadmap involving AI skilling, research and innovation, sector-specific missions, ethical oversight, monitoring mechanisms, and international collaboration. It concludes that responsible and inclusive AI adoption can significantly strengthen India’s economic capabilities, human development, self-reliance, and global leadership, thereby contributing meaningfully to the achievement of Viksit Bharat 2047.

title: Protocol pre-registration — Lontano Terremoto: response of the PASM phase-imprint observable to the lunisolar harmonic tidal field (M2/S2) on a superconducting quantum processor
abstract: Public pre-registration (N47Lab method: criteria written BEFORE the data, not negotiable afterwards) of a search for a response of the PASM (Phase-Anchored State Multiplexing) phase-imprint observable to the lunisolar harmonic tidal field on a superconducting quantum processor. Hypothesis: if the phase imprint is a property of the substrate sensitive to external gravitational stimuli, the PASM mutual information must modulate coherently with the harmonic tidal potential (constituents M2, S2, N2, K1, O1, Mf, Mm). If the imprint is insensitive to the environment, the MI spectrum is flat at tidal frequencies. No intermediate result modifies this hypothesis. Foundation (ANALOGICAL motivation, not proof): atomic clocks respond to the lunisolar tidal field (Qin & Cheng, Astron. J. 158, 262 (2019), DOI 10.3847/1538-3881/abc06f): the tidal field is a real, modeled, measurable signal on precision quantum systems. The direct channel (qubit frequency) is ~11 orders of magnitude below device noise: the analogy does NOT extend to that channel. The tested channel is the temporal statistical modulation of the PASM observable (shared MI), never evaluated in the literature (verification 31/08/2026): neither tested, nor discarded, nor considered - documentary silence, not a verdict. Method: session >= 30 days, one point every 30-60 minutes with rotated schedules (decorrelation from the solar day), fixed backend (ibm_marrakesh), 2 replicates per point, MI with timestamp, theoretical tidal reference from ephemerides (no ocean tides). Analysis: Lomb-Scargle periodogram on MI(t), significance vs null (permutations + FDR). Decision criteria (written first, not negotiable after data): C1 Presence: spectral power at M2 frequency significant vs null; C2 Discrimination: M2 and S2 resolved as distinct lines; C3 Ratio: M2/S2 power compatible with 2.17 within +/-50%; C4 Negative control: lines at NON-tidal frequencies must be absent (if present -> instrumental artifact, outcome NOT VALID). Pre-registered decision: >= 2 of 3 criteria (C1-C3) + clean C4 -> TIDAL RESPONSE; otherwise -> NOT DETECTED (environmental negative control, useful and publishable result). The test has value in both outcomes. Declared limits: hunt, not guarantee; 'NOT DETECTED' = non-detection at the given sensitivity (power, not absence); thermal drift and daily calibrations monitored and decorrelated. Context note (NOT a criterion): optional post-data coherence check - cross-correlation of MI(t) with public atomic-clock phase series (common M2 harmonic). It does NOT enter the pre-registered decision: criteria C1-C4 are the only ones. No modification to the criteria after session start, except formal ex-ante amendment. Related: MatterMemory PASM data V2 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22134568), pasm-experiments (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21830151), research-timeline (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21855315).

The tested channel is the temporal statistical modulation of the PASM observable (shared MI), never evaluated in the literature (verification 31/08/2026): neither tested, nor discarded, nor considered - documentary silence, not a verdict. Method: session >= 30 days, one point every 30-60 minutes with rotated schedules (decorrelation from the solar day), fixed backend (ibm_marrakesh), 2 replicates per point, MI with timestamp, theoretical tidal reference from ephemerides (no ocean tides). Analysis: Lomb-Scargle periodogram on MI(t), significance vs null (permutations + FDR). Decision criteria (written first, not negotiable after data): C1 Presence: spectral power at M2 frequency significant vs null; C2 Discrimination: M2 and S2 resolved as distinct lines; C3 Ratio: M2/S2 power compatible with 2.17 within +/-50%; C4 Negative control: lines at NON-tidal frequencies must be absent (if present -> instrumental artifact, outcome NOT VALID). Pre-registered decision: >= 2 of 3 criteria (C1-C3) + clean C4 -> TIDAL RESPONSE; otherwise -> NOT DETECTED (environmental negative control, useful and publishable result). The test has value in both outcomes. Declared limits: hunt, not guarantee; 'NOT DETECTED' = non-detection at the given sensitivity (power, not absence); thermal drift and daily calibrations monitored and decorrelated. Context note (NOT a criterion): optional post-data coherence check - cross-correlation of MI(t) with public atomic-clock phase series (common M2 harmonic). It does NOT enter the pre-registered decision: criteria C1-C4 are the only ones. No modification to the criteria after session start, except formal ex-ante amendment. title: From Dendrograms to Raw Sequencing: A Narrative Review of Hierarchical Clustering
abstract: Hierarchical clustering is data analysis's oldest answer to its most natural question: what is near what? This article presents a narrative review of the literature that built the field. The synthesis is organized around three themes: the taxonomic foundations, in which Sokal and Sneath's numerical taxonomy, Ward's variance-optimal grouping, and Lance and Williams's general theory of sorting strategies fixed the agglomerative canon --- single, complete, average linkage, and Ward's criterion --- as a formal discipline; the algorithmic maturity, in which Jardine and Sibson's mathematical taxonomy, Jain and Dubes's algorithms, and Kaufman and Rousseeuw's finding groups in data consolidated the methods' complexity, validity, and software; and the scaling and modern era, in which Zhang's BIRCH, Guha's CURE, and Karypis's CHAMELEON carried the hierarchy to large databases, and Murtagh's surveys and Müllner's modern analysis systematized the algorithms' practice. It is concluded that the field's literature describes a single construction --- the dendrogram as data's irreducible summary --- whose linkages are conventions, whose optimality is Ward's, and whose durability (from hand-sorted botanical tables to billion-point sequencing) comes from answering the question every cluster analysis begins with: the shape of similarity itself.

title: 自适应量子电路设计算法
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for tackling complex problems currently intractable for classical computers. However, realizing this potential requires significant advancements in quantum circuit design, particularly in terms of efficiency and scalability. This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive quantum circuit design algorithm, designed to automatically adjust quantum circuit parameters based on system performance targets. The core mechanism leverages a self-learning process, iteratively refining the circuit structure to optimize key performance indicators – including qubit count, coherence time, and fidelity – thereby enhancing the overall quantum computation efficiency. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the algorithm's ability to achieve significant performance improvements compared to traditional approaches, highlighting its potential to accelerate the development of practical quantum devices.

title: 基于量子自适应的机器学习的梯度裁剪策略
abstract: This paper introduces a novel gradient clipping strategy based on quantum self-adaptation, designed to enhance model stability in machine learning applications. Traditional gradient clipping methods rely on manual parameter tuning, which can be time-consuming and prone to suboptimal results. This work leverages quantum self-adaptation to dynamically adjust the gradient clipping parameters, resulting in more robust and stable training cycles. We present a framework incorporating quantum algorithms to efficiently manage the gradient accumulation and minimize numerical instability. The proposed method demonstrates improved convergence speed and increased model resilience compared to conventional gradient clipping techniques. We provide a detailed analysis of the algorithm's performance and discuss its potential implications for various machine learning tasks.

title: Dynamic and Explainable Deep Learning Models
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to developing dynamic and explainable deep learning models. The core challenge in deploying deep learning systems is often their "black box" nature, hindering trust and adoption. This work addresses this issue by integrating Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques with Reinforcement Learning (RL). The resulting model, termed a Dynamic Explainable Deep Learning (DEDL) model, not only produces predictions but also provides a traceable explanation of its decision-making process. Crucially, the model incorporates a feedback loop driven by user input, allowing it to adapt its parameters and improve both its predictive accuracy and the clarity of its explanations over time. The system aims to create a truly interactive and understandable AI, shifting from opaque prediction to transparent reasoning. This paper details the architecture, the learning process, and the explanation generation strategies employed within the DEDL framework. The focus is on the design principles and the core algorithms, demonstrating a pathway towards more trustworthy and adaptable deep learning systems. The system's performance is evaluated based on a combination of predictive accuracy metrics and the subjective quality of the generated explanations. The key innovation lies in the continuous interplay between explanation and learning, fostering a truly dynamic and explainable AI.

title: Title: Adaptive Clustering Algorithm based on Geometric Structure
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive clustering algorithm that leverages geometric structure to dynamically adjust cluster parameters and thresholds. Traditional clustering methods often rely on predefined parameters, limiting their flexibility and potentially hindering the ability to effectively represent complex data. This work proposes a novel approach utilizing self-adaptive learning to automatically refine the clustering process based on the inherent geometric properties of the data. The core mechanism involves adjusting the cluster threshold and model parameters iteratively, guided by a geometric feature extraction process. The goal is to enhance clustering quality, improve data representation, and achieve more robust and effective clustering results. The algorithm's effectiveness is demonstrated through a series of benchmark datasets, showcasing its adaptability and superior performance compared to existing methods. The study also explores the potential benefits of this adaptive approach in various data analysis scenarios.

title: Neuro-Lattice Modeling with Adaptive Feedback Loops
abstract: This paper introduces Neuro-Lattice Modeling with Adaptive Feedback Loops, a novel computational framework for neural network representation and control. We propose a model incorporating adaptive feedback loops that dynamically adjust synaptic connections based on observed synaptic plasticity, enabling the prediction and manipulation of complex cognitive states. The core mechanism focuses on developing a 'Lattice Stability Metric' to guide iterative adjustments, offering a potential pathway to enhancing cognitive performance. This work addresses a gap in understanding the intricate dynamics of neural networks and proposes a method for quantifying and shaping the fundamental organizational structure of the brain. We present preliminary results demonstrating the efficacy of this approach in predicting and influencing task-related behavior. The model's inherent adaptability and focus on synaptic plasticity represent a significant step towards a more nuanced and effective computational representation of cognitive processes.

title: 基于量子纠错码的分布式内存系统
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed memory system leveraging the principles of quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs) to achieve high fault tolerance. The core idea involves encoding data into a QECC, followed by employing quantum error correction algorithms for error detection and correction. This approach significantly enhances the reliability and security of data storage and transmission compared to traditional methods. We outline the system architecture, the encoding and decoding process using specific QECCs, and the error correction protocols. The system's performance is theoretically analyzed, demonstrating its potential to overcome the limitations of classical distributed memory systems in the face of noise and decoherence. The key contribution lies in the integration of QECCs directly into the design of a distributed memory system, offering a pathway towards robust quantum data storage. Further research will focus on optimizing the system for practical implementation and exploring the use of different QECCs tailored to specific application requirements.

title: 自适应拓扑场论的量子计算算法的优化
abstract: This paper investigates the optimization of quantum computation algorithms using a novel self-adaptive topology field theory (ATFT) approach. Traditional optimization methods often require manual adjustment, offering limited flexibility. This work proposes a dynamic optimization strategy leveraging quantum computing's inherent parallelism to automatically adjust the objective function, enabling efficient global optimization of complex geometric shapes. We present a theoretical framework for this optimization, demonstrating its potential to significantly improve algorithm performance compared to conventional techniques. The core mechanism centers around utilizing quantum entanglement and superposition to explore a vast solution space in parallel, facilitating a more robust and adaptable optimization process. This research explores the potential of this approach for tackling computationally challenging problems in quantum algorithm design.

abstract: This paper presents a novel high-dimensional data clustering algorithm designed to dynamically adjust clustering models based on data distribution shifts. Traditional clustering methods often lack the ability to adapt to evolving data patterns, leading to suboptimal results. Our algorithm employs an adaptive parameter adjustment mechanism utilizing a self-adaptive clustering approach. We provide a comprehensive analysis of the algorithm's performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in diverse datasets with dynamic distributions.

title: Non-Von Neumann Architectures for Neural Computation Models
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neural computation, moving beyond the limitations of traditional Von Neumann architectures. We introduce a computational model based on "neural clusters" and "synaptic networks" designed for efficient parallel computation. This model leverages the inherent parallelism of interconnected neural clusters and the dynamic adaptability of synaptic networks to achieve distributed neural computation. The core claim is that neural computation can be effectively implemented through non-Von Neumann data structures, offering a pathway to massively scalable neural computing systems. The key mechanism involves the parallel connections between neural clusters and the dynamic adjustment capabilities of the synaptic networks. This represents a fundamental shift in the architectural paradigm of neural computation, providing a new perspective for constructing large-scale neural computing systems. This work explores the theoretical foundations and potential benefits of this architecture. ---

title: Meta-Reinforcement Learning with Intrinsic Motivation for Exploration
abstract: Meta-reinforcement learning (Meta-RL) aims to develop agents capable of rapidly adapting to new tasks. However, traditional Meta-RL often relies heavily on extrinsic rewards, which can be sparse and inefficient, particularly in complex environments. This work proposes a novel approach to Meta-RL that integrates intrinsic motivation signals, such as surprise or novelty, to enhance exploration. The core idea is that an agent's inherent drive to seek out novel experiences can significantly accelerate learning and improve robustness. We introduce a framework where a meta-RL agent simultaneously learns policies for diverse tasks and receives intrinsic rewards based on the unexpectedness of its experiences. This intrinsic reward signal acts as a guiding force, pushing the agent to explore unfamiliar states and potentially leading to faster convergence and better generalization performance compared to extrinsic reward-only Meta-RL. The theoretical framework leverages concepts from information theory and Bayesian inference to formalize the intrinsic reward calculation and its impact on exploration. We demonstrate, through simulations, that incorporating intrinsic motivation leads to improved exploration and faster learning rates in challenging Meta-RL scenarios. The key contribution lies in shifting the focus from solely relying on externally provided rewards to harnessing an agent's internal drive for discovery.

title: Bioinformatics Quantum Algorithm
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum computing to revolutionize bioinformatics, specifically focusing on enhanced gene sequence analysis and protein structure prediction. The core concept centers around utilizing quantum error correction and quantum computation to accelerate these computationally intensive tasks. We propose a novel algorithm architecture leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to overcome limitations inherent in classical approaches. The paper details the design of a quantum algorithm for sequence alignment and protein folding, emphasizing the key quantum mechanisms that underpin its enhanced performance. We present a preliminary analysis of the algorithm's potential advantages, focusing on reduced computational complexity and improved accuracy compared to existing classical methods. The research highlights the significance of quantum algorithms in addressing critical challenges within the field of bioinformatics.
